STN-4W7R.title: agent-stance: attach advisory obligations to existing checkpoints

sections.Problem: Advisorship that lives only in the digest's adjectives decays under context pressure and on weaker models; nothing obliges the agent to give the expert take at the moments it matters.
sections.Proposed change:
- Attach an advisory obligation to checkpoints models already hit: plan creation (plan-shape pushback), backlog `pick` ("is this still worth doing?"), discovery start
- Add an explicit "should this be built as asked?" line to the Before-Building check
sections.Acceptance:
- [ ] Each named checkpoint carries an advisory obligation in its own surface
- [ ] The Before-Building check asks whether the work should be built as asked
sections.Scope-out: The tone half (part (a)) is delivered — the digest stance block was rewritten from a trait list to expert-take-leads framing. Do not redo it.
sections.Evidence: Parent: `framework-efficiency-review-2026-07-02.md` § "Advisor-first stance". Sole operational surface is now `methodology/session-digest.md`; `methodology/agent-stance.md` was folded and deleted.

STN-6K3D.title: agent-stance: ship an opt-in, non-forced output style

sections.Problem: Power users have no way to opt into the prawduct voice through `/config`; the stance ships only through the always-on session digest.
sections.Proposed change: - Ship `output-styles/<name>.md` with **no** `force-for-plugin` key, so it composes instead of clobbering
sections.Acceptance: - [ ] A user can select the style via `/config` without losing their own output style
sections.Scope-out: A `force-for-plugin` style. It hard-overrides a consumer's own style and does not compose — disqualifying for unconditional governance (verified against the Claude Code output-styles docs, 2026-06-04).
sections.Evidence: Low priority: the digest already delivers the stance unconditionally. This is pure ergonomics, filed from the rigor-and-stance cumulative Critic under Complete Delivery.

DOC-3V7T.title: artifacts: give review and research output a first-class home

sections.Problem: Rich review and research output has no first-class home; every cross-session surface that could carry it — build-plan Context, backlog one-liners, the session handoff — is thin, so the context is lost between sessions.
sections.Proposed change:
- A naming convention for artifacts under `.prawduct/artifacts/`
- Backlog items `refs:` their parent artifact
- `pick` surfaces the linked artifact
sections.Acceptance:
- [ ] The convention is stated in `planning.md`
- [ ] `pick` shows an item's parent artifact when one is linked
sections.Scope-out: Building machinery. The deliverable is a convention plus a template plus one line of guidance.
sections.Evidence: The 2026-07-02 efficiency review had to hand-roll this workaround for itself (write an artifact, link every item to it) — finding 6b.

BKL-4R7V.title: backlog: citation surfaces do not recognize owner/repo#number ids

sections.Problem: After cutover the canonical item id is `owner/repo#number`, but every citation-consuming surface still matches only the markdown-era `[PFX-XXXX]` spelling.
sections.Repro: Write a post-cutover item reference as `owner/repo#123` in a change-log entry or a backlog metadata bar, then run any citation-consuming check.
sections.Actual: The reference is not mis-read — it is not seen at all. Silent, with no signal to any reader.
sections.Expected: Both spellings are recognized indefinitely. Recognition is **additive**: never narrow the PFX matching — archived items keep PFX ids, `id:PFX` alias labels persist, and pre-cutover documents are not rewritten.
sections.Evidence: `lib/norm_probes.py:144` `_BACKLOG_ID_RE` is PFX-only. Same assumption behind Critic check C-B4, PR reviewer R-2, `closes:`/`closed-by:` in change-log entries and metadata bars, and the deferred backlog-id half of `lib/buildplan_refs.py`. Parent requirement GV9. Split the cheap half (widen the regexes) from resolving `#N` to a live status, which is a backlog read and lands with the W1 cache under GV8.

BKL-8Q3D.title: backlog: update stage= leaves stage-describing body prose stale

sections.Problem: Advancing an item's stage changes the `stage:` metadata field but never reconciles body prose that describes or justifies the *old* stage, so the two contradict each other.
sections.Repro: `/prawduct:backlog update <id> stage=design` on an item whose body says "`stage: requirements` is deliberate" or "do NOT route this into implementation via `pick`".
sections.Actual: The field flips; the prose still argues for the old stage. A reader who trusts the prose over the field is misrouted back to discovery.
sections.Expected: A stage change either reconciles the stage-describing prose or warns that it references the old stage.
sections.Evidence: The 2026-07-23 consolidation session left stale prose in ~5 body spots across BKL-7Q4M and BKL-9XQ2, caught only across ~3 extra backlog passes plus a Critic stale-prose warning. This is the skill's own mutation site carrying the failure the skill exists to prevent elsewhere. Related learnings: `learnings.md:109`, `:47`.

BKL-0QR1.title: backlog-service: drop-box retires before its replacement exists

sections.Problem: Retiring the `incoming-bugs/` drop-box removes the only working upstream delivery channel before XP1 exists, so consumers cannot file a prawduct bug upstream at all in the interim.
sections.Proposed change:
- Retire the drop-box **in lockstep** with a minimal same-repo replacement, never before it (owner sign-off 2026-07-17, option (c))
- `report-bug` files an `untriaged-upstream`-labeled issue into prawduct's own public repo through the adapter's create path
- The `untriaged-upstream-reports` advisory counts labeled issues instead of `incoming-bugs/*.md`
sections.Acceptance:
- [ ] The drop-box is removed only in the same change that lands its replacement
- [ ] The advisory counts labeled issues
sections.Scope-out: Full XP1. The cross-owner / foreign-identity / private-target surface stays W3. This subset needs no new auth — any authenticated user may open an issue on a public repo.
sections.Evidence: **GATED by BKL-9XQ2** since 2026-07-20: this is the first path by which a consuming repo — including a private one — sends a bug body into prawduct's public repo, so approval policy, evidence/exfiltration and label taxonomy must settle first, and the guard must bind at the adapter, not in `report-bug` prose. The non-MG5 legs of Chunk 06 are not blocked.

BKL-2K8V.title: backlog-service: pick latency ~6x the <2s floor on the gh path

sections.Problem: `pick` fetches every open `stage:ready` issue across paginated `gh` subprocess calls on every call, and that fixed full-scan cost keeps the NFR <2s floor out of reach.
sections.Repro: SPIKE-S2 live dry-run, 2026-07-17, ~209-issue throwaway repo.
sections.Actual: `pick_latency_ms_by_candidates` measured {1: 12528, 3: 12390, 5: 12380} — ~12.4s, ~6x the target.
sections.Expected: The <2s floor requires the raw-HTTP/GraphQL fast-path (W1) or a scoped candidate query that avoids the full-issue scan. It is not slice-native.
sections.Evidence: **The "flat across candidates ⇒ not N+1" reading is RETRACTED and the retraction is the reusable part**: the probe varied `limit`, which `pick` applied *after* fanning out over every eligible issue, so flatness was guaranteed by construction and carried no information. Chunk 05b (`2ee2a17`) then made `pick` rank first and take dependency reads lazily in rank order, so the candidate parameterization is finally meaningful — read the *slope*, not the magnitude. Remaining scope is the `_all_issues` full-scan floor only, and it is W1-gated.

BKL-3H7W.title: backlog-service: the REST-point meter under-counts paged reads

sections.Problem: `_PacingTransport` charges one point per attribute-call, but `GhTransport._api_paged` issues up to 100 HTTP requests inside a single call, so every paged read is charged once regardless of page count.
sections.Repro: A ~300-item `--archive-scope all` run: `_create_item` calls `provision.ensure_labels()` → `transport.list_labels()` per item, and label listing grows from 1 to ~4 pages.
sections.Actual: ~700 actual label-listing requests while 295 points are charged — roughly a 7% under-count, growing with backlog size.
sections.Expected: Either the meter charges per request, or all three surfaces stop claiming it charges every REST call.
sections.Evidence: Scoped honestly: **an under-count, not an unmetered path** — every write method is single-request, so no write escapes the meter and the shortfall is reads only. Three durable surfaces claim a completeness the mechanism lacks and must be corrected with the fix: `migrate.py:270-273`, `backlog-service-nfr.md:146`, and the VRF-009 record at `operator-verification.md:347`. VRF-009's `rest_points_charged: 5360` is therefore a **floor**; the qualitative "budgets never bind under serial I/O" conclusion survives, since under-counting cannot manufacture a false no-waits result.

BKL-4T9C.title: backlog-service: the no-self-file check is fail-open by default

sections.Problem: The check that stops prawduct's own repo self-filing keys off `backlog_service_repo`, which is unset in every pre-cutover repo — an invariant whose default value disables it.
sections.Repro: Any repo that has not run the cutover: `backlog_service_repo` is unset, so the comparison in `upstream-filing.md` §5 check 3 has nothing to match.
sections.Actual: Structurally inert exactly where it matters, and inert by default.
sections.Expected: Identity resolves from **both** `backlog_service_repo` and the git remote; the check refuses if **either** matches the pinned target, and **fails closed** when neither resolves.
sections.Evidence: **APPROVED and landed as a design amendment 2026-07-24** — `backlog-service-upstream-filing.md` §5 carries the `[AMENDMENT]` block. `lib/backlog/context.py` performs no git-remote resolution (it resolves *execution* context, not repo identity), so the state scalar was the adapter's only self-identity signal. Sequencing consequence: **Chunk 08a no longer depends on Chunk 06/07** and is buildable offline against `tests/fakes/fake_github.py`; 08b still needs the live target.

BKL-4Z7M.title: backlog-service: a skipped archive is unreachable and unsignalled

sections.Problem: Items excluded by `--archive-scope open` are not on the service at all, and after cutover the skill treats the source markdown as frozen history — so post-cutover `list` and add-time dedup silently omit them, with nothing surfacing that state to the user.
sections.Repro: Migrate with `--archive-scope open`, then file an item duplicating a previously-dropped archived one.
sections.Actual: No signal that the project already considered and rejected it. A repo can sit indefinitely with an un-backfilled archive and no indication a one-command backfill exists.
sections.Expected: The condition is surfaced — the adapter or the session briefing detects an `open`-migrated repo with an un-backfilled archive and points at the `--archive-scope all` re-run.
sections.Evidence: **Recoverable, not data loss** (verified 2026-07-20): a re-run under `all` backfills without duplicating, on the authority of the `id:PFX` alias written atomically in the create — guarded by `tests/test_backlog_migrate.py::TestArchiveScope::test_open_then_all_backfills_the_archive_without_duplicating`. Severity is discoverability, not permanence. **Not a `find` claim**: post-cutover full-text `find` is W2-deferred for every item; the gaps are additive, and W2 inherits this one. prawduct itself is unaffected (A1 chose `all`), so this is adopter-facing.

BKL-5Q9C.title: backlog-service: pick can return an item closed seconds earlier

sections.Problem: The close→list path has no settle-retry for GitHub's replication window, though the create→get path already has one for the same class of gap.
sections.Repro: `status <id> --to shipped`, then immediately `pick` — the single most common transition in the tool's intended loop.
sections.Actual: `pick` returns the just-closed item, with nothing marking the result as stale. Re-running seconds later is correct.
sections.Expected: A bounded settle-retry re-queries when a returned candidate's local state says closed.
sections.Evidence: **Correctly diagnosed as a replication window, not a filter bug — this distinction is the whole item and a fix aimed at the filter would be wrong.** At the moment of the stale read GitHub was already correct: the issue carried `state: closed` with `closed_at` set, and a direct `issues?state=open&labels=stage:ready` query already excluded it. The list endpoint served a stale page. Reuse `core.py:296`'s existing budget discipline rather than inventing a second retry policy — and note BKL-4H8P's warning that a retry contract with no stated max is what produced an unbounded loop before, so the budget must be explicit at the contract.

BKL-6M4T.title: backlog-service: run the live prawduct backlog migration

sections.Problem: The offline deliverables landed 2026-07-17; the live, owner-in-the-loop migration of prawduct's own backlog has never run.
sections.Proposed change:
- Run the MG4 scrub against the owner-confirmed dispositions
- Bulk import (`backlog.md` + archive → issues), idempotent and resumable, keyed on the `id:PFX` alias
- Repoint the briefing and gates through the adapter
- Record VRF-006 with a rollback note
sections.Acceptance:
- [ ] `verify-migration` exits 0 with all five conflict lists empty
- [ ] `get`/`list`/`pick` resolve real PFX ids and counts reconcile
- [ ] `backlog_service_repo` is set and the cutover is recorded
sections.Scope-out: **`legacy.py` retirement is struck.** GV7 and MG3 both retire it only when the whole portfolio has migrated, not at any one project's cutover — and `lib/backlog/migrate.py` reads the source through `legacy.parse_backlog`, so retiring it would disable the next repo's migration. **The MG5 drop-box leg stays gated** by BKL-9XQ2 (see BKL-0QR1).
sections.Evidence: Scrub dispositions, restructure scope and `--archive-scope all` are owner-approved in `artifacts/migration-scrub-decisions.md`. At cutover, update `artifacts/architecture.md` (the `lib/backlog` component, the `gh` runtime dependency, the clone-shared counts store, the briefing/gate repoint) and note `gh` in the preferences dependency inventory.

BKL-6W9R.title: backlog-service: page-cap trips are silent truncation in 4 loops

sections.Problem: When `_api_paged` hits `_PAGED_MAX_PAGES` it returns the collected prefix indistinguishably from completion, and four near-identical paginators carry divergent bounds and cap-trip loudness.
sections.Repro: An endpoint with more than 100 pages of results (labels, timeline, sub-issues) — reachable at 10k+ entries.
sections.Actual: The truncated prefix is returned as if complete. `export` — the MG2 backup — cannot distinguish truncated from complete.
sections.Expected: A cap trip raises `TransportError(unavailable, 'result truncated at N pages')` or surfaces a warning through the envelope.
sections.Evidence: A partial fix landed 2026-07-18: `core.iter_alias_issues` is bounded by `_ALIAS_SCAN_MAX_PAGES=100` with a diag line on cap trip. **The remaining direction is the one worth the item**: extract ONE shared issue-list paginator to replace the four near-identical loops (`transport._api_paged`, `query._all_issues`, `migrate._scan_all`, `core.iter_alias_issues`) and converge their bounds — one place to fail loud instead of four divergent caps. Not migration-gating at prawduct's scale.

BKL-6X5D.title: backlog-service: quantify the archive window between all and open

sections.Problem: The only shipped archive lever is the binary `--archive-scope {all,open}`. The quantified middle — migrate the last N months, drop older — has never been specified, so adopters at scale have no proportionate option.
sections.Proposed change:
- Define an N-months or throughput formula between the two poles
- **Close any window over its own references before import** — a window is a starting selection, not the final set
sections.Acceptance:
- [ ] A stated formula, with the reference-closure step specified
- [ ] No live item can reference an excluded target
sections.Scope-out: Part (b) — metering the create+close stretch — **BUILT 2026-07-24** in Chunk 04 via the `_PacingTransport` decorator. Part (a)'s doc-coherence legs closed 2026-07-20 across six surfaces. Do not redo either.
sections.Evidence: **The measurement killed the status-keyed pole this nearly shipped with.** The candidate middle was "keep open + dropped, discard shipped", reasoning that shipped work is safe in git history. Measured against the real corpus that is backwards: archived *shipped* items carry substantial bodies and a clear majority are referenced by live work, at a far higher rate than archived *dropped* items — and shipped is much the larger set, so the pole would have preserved the small set and discarded the one live work points at. Re-derive with `tests/spikes/backlog_archive_value.py`; do not cite digits.

BKL-7D3V.title: backlog-service: lift the migration-required advisory in code

sections.Problem: The owner decided 2026-07-24 that `backlog-service-migration-required` ships **lifted**, but the code still registers the held no-op, so the flagship feature stays invisible to every consumer.
sections.Proposed change:
- Register `probe_migration_required` directly in `lib/backlog_probes.py` `register()` in place of `_probe_migration_required_held`
- Delete the `_probe_migration_required_held` no-op wrapper
- Flip `tests/test_backlog_probes.py::TestMigrationRequiredProbe::test_held_out_of_live_roster` back to asserting the live roster
- Correct the module and `register()` docstrings, both of which describe the hold
sections.Acceptance: - [ ] The live roster surfaces the advisory and the test pins that, not the hold
sections.Scope-out: Re-litigating the decision. The recorded deliverable — an owner decision rather than the probe's default deciding — is satisfied; what remains is implementation (Chunk 07 done-when #5).
sections.Evidence: **Accepted risks, recorded so they are not rediscovered as surprises.** BKL-8W2M is unbuilt, so a repo that will never host on GitHub gets an unresolvable `warn` every session and per-user dismissal does not survive a fresh clone — that item is what makes the lift survivable. And the proof is n=1 on prawduct-shaped data. **Why the hold existed at all** (merged from BKL-6J2X): lifting is not a cosmetic default flip — it is an automated route from every consuming repo into an irreversible bulk write of 100–250 real issues.

BKL-7F3D.title: backlog-service: ship YAML Issue Forms for consumer UI filers

sections.Problem: Humans filing through the GitHub UI have nothing enforcing the issue standard's sections at creation.
sections.Proposed change:
- Ship YAML Issue Forms in `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE`, one per variant (bug, task/feature)
- Required textareas = the standard's hard section list; dropdowns pin `kind`/`area`/`stage`/`impact`
- `labels:` auto-applies defaults (`provision` already creates the labels)
sections.Acceptance: - [ ] A UI-filed issue arrives with the required sections and the pinned facets
sections.Scope-out: Gating programmatic creation. Forms only gate UI-created issues; prawduct's own `file` path is governed by BKL-2H9W and BKL-4C6P, both shipped. Markdown templates only as a fallback for repos that will not adopt forms.
sections.Evidence: This is the consumer-facing enforcement home named by `documentation/backlog-service-issue-standard.md` §4. It carries the entire residual of the decomposed BKL-3T7X.

BKL-7Q4M.title: backlog-service: build the content-minimizing upstream filing path

sections.Problem: A private consuming repo cannot file a prawduct bug into prawduct's public repo without risking leaking its own content. The written security design answers *who may file where*; it does not answer **which fields cross the boundary**.
sections.Proposed change: - Build against the owner-approved design in `documentation/backlog-service-upstream-filing.md`, which settles the outbound-payload shape against requirements XP4–XP7
sections.Acceptance:
- [ ] The outbound payload is allowlist-shaped and the owner sees it before it is sent
- [ ] `tests/preferences/test_no_upstream_content_egress.py` is deliberately superseded, not quietly deleted
sections.Scope-out: Re-drafting a parallel security model. `backlog-service-security-model.md` already covers auth by target owner (§1), untrusted-until-triaged arrivals (§5), abuse prevention (§6) and cross-owner cache scoping (§4). Start by reading those.
sections.Evidence: **RELEASE BLOCKER for 3.2.0 (owner, 2026-07-21), and the tracking item for a live norm exception.** `security-model.md` § Direction — "a governed product's content never leaves that product's own repository and owner" — is `Status: in-transition` citing this item by name, and its interim enforcement test stays live until a design deliberately supersedes it. **Deliberately separate from BKL-9XQ2, not merged**: that item is the broad consent/attribution/taxonomy question, this is specifically the content-minimization leg, and the norm's citation must keep resolving.

BKL-8H2W.title: backlog-service: no durable owner-confirmation gate in the CLI

sections.Problem: The durable fix for the model-initiated destructive path — a confirmation gate in the CLI that binds regardless of caller — is named as debt only in a change-log entry, and its sole tracking pointer archives at the Chunk 09 flip.
sections.Proposed change: - Design and build a CLI-level confirmation gate that binds any caller, not just the skill
sections.Acceptance: - [ ] The gate fires for an operator or a runbook invoking the CLI directly, not only through the skill
sections.Scope-out: Nothing here re-opens the skill-level narrowing that already shipped in `85753fd`. `stage: design` is deliberate — what the gate confirms (blast radius, irreversibility, op scope), how it behaves non-interactively, and how it relates to `restructure-preview` are open questions.
sections.Evidence: **The defect is the reference, not the debt.** A grant narrowing bounds *who may call*; it does not bound *what the call does* — the same distinction BKL-9XQ2 records ("permissions bound who may call, not where the call may send"). This gate is also the concrete mechanism that would satisfy the amended operation-level approval norm at the data plane rather than in prose. **Second "named as debt with nothing holding it" instance in one day** — a change-log sentence saying "this is named debt, not a silent omission" is only true if something durable holds it.

BKL-8W2M.title: backlog-service: no terminal-markdown state, so the nudge never ends

sections.Problem: `probe_migration_required` has exactly one resolution condition — `backlog_service_repo` being set. A product deliberately staying on markdown forever (no GitHub remote, a non-GitHub forge, an owner who does not want an Issues tracker) has no way to resolve the advisory, because the only exit is adopting the thing it will never adopt.
sections.Proposed change:
- Decide whether terminal-markdown is a first-class supported state or an unsupported edge
- If first-class, decide how it is declared and whether it silences the rest of the migration-shaped surface
sections.Acceptance: - [ ] A repo that will never host on GitHub has a recorded, committed way to stop the nudge
sections.Scope-out: Plain advisory *dismissal* is probably not the answer — a permanent architectural fact deserves a recorded, shared, committed state, not a per-user dismissal every fresh clone re-nags about.
sections.Evidence: **`stage: requirements` is deliberate — this is a product decision before it is code.** Impact raised M→L by owner decision 2026-07-24: with the advisory shipping **lifted** (BKL-7D3V), the hold that was masking this permanent case is being retired, so the failure mode moves from hypothetical to shipped fleet-wide. **This is now the item that makes the lift survivable** and should be scheduled immediately behind v3.2.0 if it misses the release.

BKL-9F6T.title: backlog-service: a scrub survey records no coverage boundary

sections.Problem: A migration scrub survey is a claim about a corpus **at a moment**, and neither `migration-scrub.md` nor any artifact it writes records *which moment*. With no recorded coverage boundary there is no definition of "surveyed", so an approved disposition table has unknown currency at the one moment it must be trustworthy.
sections.Repro: Approve a disposition table, let the corpus grow, then run the migration against it.
sections.Actual: Dispositions approved 2026-07-18; by 2026-07-31, 91 items sat outside every recorded disposition, never screened at all. Caught only because someone hand-built `tests/spikes/backlog_scrub_drift.py` — and `tests/` is in `NOT_DISTRIBUTED_DIRS`, so **every consumer following the runbook has no drift check whatsoever**.
sections.Expected: The disposition table carries a written survey baseline; the unsurveyed set is re-derived against it and reported at Step 3 as a stated choice.
sections.Evidence: **Three defects in the one instrument that exists, none of which the fix may reproduce.** (1) Its baseline is a hardcoded git ref and "unsurveyed" is *items filed since that ref*, so on a growing corpus `verdict: CURRENT` was **structurally unreachable** until a survey covered the whole corpus. (2) **A git-ref baseline dies at cutover** — it resolves via `git show <ref>:<backlog>`, so it silently stops meaning anything at exactly the transition it guards. Make the baseline a **date**: every open markdown item carries `added:` and issues carry `created_at`. (3) A short SHA is fragile — BKL-2Q7F already lost one to a `git commit --amend` eighteen seconds later. Surface it as a stated choice, **not a refusal**: a survey is judgment, so a hard gate would block sound runs. **Zero new adapter op** — `list --json` plus a date filter, which matters because GOV-6D4Q forbids adding governed surface.

BKL-9J3F.title: backlog-service: four human-UI edits degrade silently in the decoder

sections.Problem: Several edits a human makes in the GitHub UI are decoded to a wrong or empty value with no warning, where the decoder should complain.
sections.Repro: In the GitHub UI: close an issue as duplicate; delete a soft-facet label such as `impact:high`; delete an item's `prawduct:` body block wholesale.
sections.Actual: (1) ENC-6 — `superseded_by` is read only from the block, never the timeline (`decode_item` never calls `list_timeline`), so a UI close-as-duplicate silently drops the redirect. (2) A deleted soft-facet label decodes to `None` with no warning. (3) ENC-5(c)'s missing-stage advisory is unimplemented. (4) A wholesale block deletion yields an empty `Block`, silently losing `id_aliases`/`superseded_by`/`claimed_at`.
sections.Expected: Each of these warns rather than degrading to a confident wrong value.
sections.Evidence: Found in the same CC5 trace as BKL-4W7H and captured there so they were not lost; filed as their own item once BKL-4W7H shipped. (1) compounds with BKL-5R2K.

BKL-9J3F.note: Four independent decoder gaps that happen to share a trace.

BKL-9XQ2.title: backlog-service: settle consent and taxonomy for upstream filing

sections.Problem: A consuming repo filing an issue against prawduct's tracker is underspecified in three ways: per-report consent, what evidence rides along, and the label taxonomy arriving issues carry.
sections.Proposed change:
- Bind the three-state policy (`always-file`/`ask-user`/`never-file`, default `ask-user`) at the **adapter — the data plane**, never in skill prose
- Settle the arriving-issue taxonomy against the namespaced `<facet>:value` labels the adapter already models, and GV6's coexistence reconcile
sections.Acceptance:
- [ ] A foreign-owner `--repo` is refused or prompted by the adapter, not by prose
- [ ] The policy is honored in the unattended path, where `ask-user` means *don't file*
sections.Scope-out: Consent-at-install. **Resolved 2026-07-23 as NOT required** — there is no install-time opt-in and no onboarding disclosure surface; per-report consent is the entire mechanism, and `always-file` is standing consent.
sections.Evidence: **THIS GATES RELEASE (owner, 2026-07-20).** The capability already exists and is merely *uninstructed*, not prevented: `backlog file --repo owner/repo` accepts **any** owner/repo — `ids.parse_repo` validates shape only, with no allowlist at any of the ten call sites. **The real risk is AGENCY AND ATTRIBUTION, not secrecy**: the adapter inherits the session's GitHub auth (PRD O5), so an issue is filed **as the user**, in someone else's public project, and GitHub has no ordinary issue-delete and never reuses numbers — so it cannot be withdrawn, only closed. **Public is not the safe-by-default case.** Scoping so the gate does not over-block: **BLOCK** Chunk 06's MG5 leg and any release carrying it; **DO NOT BLOCK** a consumer migrating its own backlog to its own Issues.

BLD-4Q8W.title: build-plan: decide if builders run verify-chunk-refs before done

sections.Problem: The concerns registry claimed `building.md` instructs builders to run `verify-chunk-refs` before marking a chunk done. That was never true — `methodology/` mentions the command nowhere. The registry cell is corrected; the decision it papered over is not made.
sections.Proposed change:
- Decide whether a builder-stage run is the right coverage or Critic-only is correct by design
- Whichever way it goes, make `cross-cutting-concerns.md:36` match reality
sections.Acceptance: - [ ] The decision is recorded, and the registry cell states what is actually true
sections.Scope-out: Building it before the decision. `stage: requirements` is deliberate — the deliverable is a decision plus, if yes, a one-paragraph methodology edit.
sections.Evidence: **Both arguments are real.** For: the Critic exit is BLOCKING, so a `missing-ref:` at review time bounces an already-declared-done chunk and the stop hook holds the session — catching it at the builder's own step is cheaper. Against: it duplicates a check the Critic runs unconditionally, and cuts against Independent Review (Principle 14). Note this whole family is a standing stream of **false** positives, so putting a cry-wolf checker in the builder's hands is a habituation risk where habituation is least recoverable. Settle it *before* BLD-8R3T changes the false-positive profile, since that profile is the main argument against.

BLD-5R7K.title: build-plan: git-derived chunk progress has an undocumented precondition

sections.Problem: Correct git-derived progress requires two things a product must happen to do — `Chunk NN` in the commit subject, and a conventional-commit scope matching the plan's `scope:` frontmatter — and neither is written down anywhere.
sections.Repro: A repo without the commit-subject habit, on a `views_enabled` branch mid-release.
sections.Actual: Falls back to the checkbox reading, which under `[ ]`-until-release is known-wrong and typically reports Chunk 01 forever. `ChunkProgress.git_derived` records which reading answered but has **no production reader** — the only reference outside the module is a test assertion.
sections.Expected: The precondition is documented where authors meet it, and the degradation announces itself.
sections.Evidence: **The generality finding is why this is worth an item**: it works here because this repo has the habit, which is exactly the shape that ships a framework mechanism correct for its author and quietly wrong for everyone else. Note the scope filter is applied **only when it matches something** — a deliberate softening, since a strict filter would have erased this repo's own signal, and a second reason the mechanism can be half-right unnoticed. Two-part fix: document the precondition in the build-plan template and `building.md` (which needs a **relocation**, not an addition — it sits at its token ceiling), and announce the degradation from a deliberately-invoked diagnostic rather than the hot path.

BLD-5V8F.title: build-plan: extend verify-chunk-refs beyond file paths

sections.Problem: v1.4 Chunk 02 shipped file-path verification only; the original plan also called for symbol and backlog-ID verification, both deferred.
sections.Proposed change:
- Define matching rules: substring grep across configured source roots for symbols; a `backlog_id_pattern` preference for backlog refs
- Extend `_parse_build_plan_chunk_refs` to return `symbols` and `backlog_refs` alongside `file_paths`
sections.Acceptance: - [ ] A build plan citing a symbol or a backlog id that does not exist is reported
sections.Scope-out: Strict symbol matching. Symbols in prose are often approximate (`parse_func` vs `_parse_func`), so a strict grep produces false positives and needs fuzzy matching — which is the reason for the original deferral.
sections.Evidence: **The backlog-ID half is newly actionable and the reason has changed twice.** The original deferral said "this project's backlog has no formal IDs" — obsolete since the `[PFX-XXXX]` migration, and doubly obsolete after the Issues cutover, where the canonical id becomes `owner/repo#number`. Sequence with BKL-4R7V, which widens every id regex, and BLD-3M7K, which wants the same token *excluded* from the file-path heuristic — complementary, and they must land coherently.

BLD-8R3T.title: build-plan: the `new` forward-ref exemption never expires

sections.Problem: The `new` qualifier correctly exempts a file a chunk will create — but the exemption is unconditional with respect to chunk completion, so once a chunk is done, a declared-new deliverable that is still absent is never existence-checked.
sections.Repro: Ship a chunk that declares `new \`lib/foo.py\`` and never creates it, or whose path is later renamed.
sections.Actual: Silenced permanently. The corpus check for BLD-6T4R found exactly two such refs — `lib/backlog.py` and `methodology/agent-stance.md`, both in `[x]` chunks, neither on disk — **true positives**, caught only incidentally because those chunks happened to re-reference the path, the very re-reference the fix suppresses.
sections.Expected: The exemption applies only while the chunk is open; once complete, `new`-declared paths are existence-checked normally.
sections.Evidence: **Two edges to watch before building.** (a) Checkboxes are a **derived view** that stays `[ ]` on a feature branch until release, so "unchecked" is not reliably "in flight" — fail toward the exemption there. Re-derive against `resolve_chunk_progress`, not "first unchecked box", and decide *deliberately* which completion the exemption expires on; `lib/gates.py:744` is a live precedent that kept the checkbox reading on purpose. (b) **The trigger surface is wider than "declared deliverable"** — the regex matches `new` before ANY backticked path, adjectival prose included, so constrain its shape at the same time (require the match to sit inside a Deliverables list item). **Merged: BLD-9H2M** (a soft-wrapped `new` is never *recognized*, because the regex is applied one line at a time — widening the exemption's reach cannot help when nothing enters the set) and **BLD-5N7C** (the two concrete stale paths above, whose fix is to annotate each with its successor rather than delete it).

BLD-ZQ2V.title: build-plan: the gate inspects the earliest incomplete chunk

sections.Problem: Every consumer treats "current chunk" as a proxy for "the chunk being worked on right now", and those two diverge the moment work proceeds out of order.
sections.Repro: Build Chunks 05, 05b and 05c while Chunk 01 is legitimately still open, then run `verify-chunk-refs`.
sections.Actual: The gate inspects Chunk 01 and nothing else, for the whole release, and reports `ok`. Chunk 01 carries exactly **1** ref, so the entire v3.2.0 release has been verifying one file reference.
sections.Expected: The gate resolves the chunk **whose refs are in the working diff**, falling back to first-incomplete only when that is empty.
sections.Evidence: **Chunk 01 is the right answer to the wrong question** — it is genuinely incomplete, so "first incomplete" correctly returns it. A fix addressing only the checkbox/commit union would leave the gate on Chunk 01 throughout out-of-order work. **Verified the git-aware path is NOT degraded here**: `resolve_chunk_progress` returns `git_derived=True` and still resolves 01, because both union legs fail (the box never flips under `[ ]`-until-release, and the completing work landed in a prior merge behind the base). **The plugin-root half of this item is SHIPPED** — `build_plan_ref_root` (`buildplan_refs.py`, `REF_ROOT_KEY`) gives declared repos a second resolution root, so the 17 plugin-relative refs across seven chunks no longer surface as blocking when current-chunk resolution is fixed. What remains is current-chunk resolution plus excluding `owner/repo` and `owner/repo#N` slugs from the file-path heuristic (4 occurrences, not reachable by the ref-root fallback). Requirements are written in `artifacts/buildplan-chunk-refs-discovery.md`.

CRT-9R4K.title: critic: defer per-chunk reviews on short plans to one cumulative

sections.Problem: For a multi-chunk feature every chunk gets its own opus Critic review and the cumulative then re-reviews all of them. On **short** plans that redundancy is the biggest avoidable wall-clock cost.
sections.Proposed change:
- Pin the eligibility bounds first: proposal is chunk-count ≤ 3 AND risk tier standard AND never escalate-tier
- Add the eligibility predicate to `lib/critic_mode.py` and the deferral to the build cycle
- Resolve how a deferred plan interacts with the stop-hook gate and session boundaries
sections.Acceptance: - [ ] A regression test proves a NON-eligible plan (4+ chunks or escalate-tier) still gets per-chunk reviews
sections.Scope-out: Shipping without that guardrail. **It is load-bearing, not a nicety** — the retired PR trivial fast-path failed precisely because it shipped with zero adversarial coverage, and a skip-gate needs the MOST adversarial coverage.
sections.Evidence: **The USER owns this tradeoff (Principle 23)**: deferring per-chunk reviews trades early detection for a bigger blast radius — a flaw introduced in chunk 1 surfaces only at end-of-plan. The 2026-06-22 chunk-mode yield (~1 actionable across 7 reviews) is **mild supporting evidence only**; early-detection value is not captured by finding-count, so this is a judgment call, not a data verdict.

LNG-5W8R.title: compliance: retire the canary checks that re-implement a linter

sections.Problem: Two of the four compliance-canary checks re-derive a linter's rules per language, so they false-positive on non-Python repos and fail open everywhere else. Prawduct should judge whether the right tools are applied, not re-implement them.
sections.Proposed change:
- **Check 3 (broad exceptions) → delete**: ruff `E722`/`BLE001`, clippy, SwiftLint and Roslyn already do it properly, and the judgment half is owned twice over by the review protocol and the preferences Enforcement table
- **Check 1 (source changed, no tests) → delete**: Critic Goal 1 covers test adequacy, and `_is_test_file` makes it a noise generator off Python/JS
- **Check 2 → keep, extend** the manifest table with `Package.swift`, `*.csproj`/`*.sln`, `CMakeLists.txt`
- **Check 4 → keep**, already language-agnostic
sections.Acceptance:
- [ ] The violation inventory is **complete first** — it gates everything else
- [ ] ruff is configured for prawduct itself before check 3 is deleted, or the check is simply lost
- [ ] `test-reference-verify` reports **unchecked** for a language it cannot analyse, so a BLOCKING Goal 1 gate can never read as satisfied by having skipped everything
- [ ] Surviving findings emit a ledger fact
- [ ] `discovery.md` asks, per ecosystem present, which checker is standard
sections.Scope-out: Prawduct writing any product code, config or tooling — including `ruff.toml` in a governed repo; running any linter; or encoding any language's *syntax* (suffix matching is fine, grammar patterns are not).
sections.Evidence: **Two confirmed sites live outside `compliance.py`** and the more serious is `bin/test-reference-verify` (`_PY_SYMBOL_RE`, `_is_python_file`), because it feeds `verify-coverage`, a BLOCKING Goal 1 check that therefore reads as satisfied on a Swift/Rust/C# repo having inspected nothing. **The measurability defect outlives all four checks**: canary findings are strings printed into the briefing and never persisted, so the control can never be retired on evidence, only defended on principle.

LNG-5W8R.note: Eight ordered acceptance criteria spanning retire, extend, configure and measure. Criterion 1 gates the rest.

COV-2P7F.title: coverage: route the change-log entry gate through judgeable_files

sections.Problem: `lib/coverage.py`'s `non_md = [f for f in files if not f.endswith(".md")]` is the last behavioral `.endswith(".md")` classifier in the gate surface, and it contradicts the doc-only gate on the same diff.
sections.Repro: A branch changing only `.prawduct/project-state.yaml` and `.prawduct/*.md`; run `check-pr-doc-only` and `check-change-log-entry`.
sections.Actual: Doc-only says `none judgeable`, rc=0. The change-log gate says `no-entry: branch changes code (.prawduct/project-state.yaml)`, rc=1. **The two gates openly contradict each other.** The inverse also holds: a branch changing only `skills/pr/SKILL.md` is `not-doc-only` yet needs no change-log entry, so behavioral skill-prose can merge unrecorded.
sections.Expected: One predicate. Change that line to `coverage_algebra.judgeable_files(files)`.
sections.Evidence: **Residual work is ONE LINE.** Most of the original umbrella is already fixed by kernel-v3 — `check-pr-doc-only` routes through `judgeable_files`, and the cumulative-critic staleness concept is gone entirely (a wholly-non-judgeable interval is a free edge). **Do NOT port the archived branch's helpers** (`is_doc_or_metadata`, `is_nonbehavioral_path`) — they are semantically identical to `is_judgeable_path` negated, so porting re-introduces the duplicate predicate CRT-5D8Q exists to kill. `tests/test_change_log_entry_gate.py` has neither a `.prawduct/`-only nor a `skills/*.md` case; the gap is untested in both directions. Resolve alongside PR-4V2N, which decides whether a `.prawduct/`-only PR even reaches this gate.

COV-4M2J.title: coverage: the coverage floor is Python-only

sections.Problem: `bin/test-reference-verify`'s symbol-grep only understands Python symbols, so on a polyglot or non-Python repo the framework's "the tests actually referenced the changed code" guarantee does not exist.
sections.Proposed change: - Decide the plug-point: a declared per-language verifier command, a built-in multi-language symbol grep, or ingesting native coverage output (lcov / cobertura)
sections.Acceptance: - [ ] A non-Python product gets the coverage guarantee without hand-rolling a verifier
sections.Scope-out: Nothing regresses today — `coverage_required` defaults OFF, so a non-Python repo yields an honest empty `changes_referenced` rather than a false failure. The current escape is bring-your-own-verifier via `--merge-into`.
sections.Evidence: **A third consumer of this root cause appeared 2026-08-01: `changes_referenced` is no longer only a coverage input.** `_GREEN_IS_EVIDENCE_DIRECTIVE` triggers off it, so it is dark in every non-Python product — and per LRN-2D7Q that directive class is the *only proven path* by which prawduct delivers a general learning into a consuming product. Filed as **GOV-6X2N** rather than folded in, because it may be closable by re-triggering off a language-agnostic signal with no language-aware floor in existence, and should not wait on this item's L-sized requirements pass. Noted here so this design knows the symbol now has a **governance** consumer as well as a coverage one.

COV-5H3N.title: coverage: resolve-base ignores origin/HEAD and defaults to main

sections.Problem: When `base_branch:` is unset, `_resolve_base_branch` falls back to a hardcoded candidate list and returns the first that resolves — even when the repo's declared default branch is `develop`.
sections.Repro: Any gitflow repo that has not set the `base_branch` knob; open its first PR.
sections.Actual: A 2-commit feature off develop is reviewed and gated as the entire develop..main promotion range. Reported from Discodon at v2.1.4; **every gitflow consumer hits it on their first PR unless they know the knob exists**. This repo masks it, because `base_branch: develop` is set.
sections.Expected: The default consults `git symbolic-ref --short refs/remotes/origin/HEAD` before the hardcoded list and prefers it when it resolves and is not main-family; and onboarding/migration sets `base_branch:` when origin/HEAD is non-main.
sections.Evidence: **More load-bearing now, not less.** The stamp-merged branch-guard consequence is retired (no flow calls `stamp-merged`), but `/prawduct:pr` create-flow Step 1d branches trunk-vs-gitflow on resolve-base — so a wrong default base silently misroutes the PR's change-log bookkeeping (statusless-until-release vs shipped-in-PR) on top of the review-scope inflation.

COV-8R2K.title: coverage: the floor blocks on prose and non-code config files

sections.Problem: The symbol-grep coverage floor is applied to non-executable files the same as code, so a chunk whose deliverables legitimately include prose or a YAML config takes an unsoftenable BLOCKING missing-coverage.
sections.Repro: Write `NOTES.md` (or edit `project-state.yaml`) on an otherwise-clean branch with `coverage_required: true`, then run `verify-coverage`.
sections.Actual: rc=1, `missing-coverage: NOTES.md`. Verified by executing develop's own suite — `tests/test_verify_coverage_gate.py:186-206` asserts exactly this. The protocol half is unfixed too: `review-protocol.md:65` still says missing-coverage lines are BLOCKING per file and must not be softened.
sections.Expected: Non-executable files are exempted or downgraded to a NOTE; an uncovered `.py` still blocks.
sections.Evidence: **Reachability — why it looks dormant but is not**: a freshly-run stock verifier routes non-Python into `changes_unjudged`, masking the symptom. It is reachable whenever `changes_unjudged` does not align with the gate's recomputed changed set — stale evidence, product-authored evidence, legacy evidence, or a `coverage_level: executed` verifier. **Load-bearing design constraint: express the exemption in terms of `is_judgeable_path`, not as a fresh suffix frozenset** — a second file-classification set is exactly the divergence CRT-5D8Q was created to kill. **Merged: COV-6T3P**, the same predicate from the opposite direction — `is_judgeable_path` hard-codes ".md is not judgeable unless governance-protected", which is right for code products and wrong for one whose *product is* the markdown, so their core work would never require review coverage. One knob answers both; COV-6T3P's open questions (binary vs path-scoped, interaction with the doc-only fast-path, whether flipping it retroactively stales composed coverage) need owner input before design.

COV-9B4T.title: coverage: prefer the nearer integration base when local is ahead

sections.Problem: Base resolution always prefers `origin/<b>` for a stable merge-base, which produces a false `uncovered` when local `<b>` is ahead of the remote and is an ancestor of HEAD.
sections.Proposed change: - Spike whether to prefer the nearer of local `<b>` / `origin/<b>` under exactly that condition
sections.Acceptance: - [ ] A decision recorded either way, with the stability tradeoff stated
sections.Scope-out: Treating this as a quick change. It is load-bearing across **every** gate that resolves a base — PR, doc-only, cumulative-critic — so it is a spike.
sections.Evidence: This is fix-shape #3 from COV-7K4N, deferred at that item's close. **Lower urgency now**: COV-7K4N's diagnostic hint plus the unpromoted-release-prep advisory already convert the wrong, expensive remedy into the right cheap one and nudge before the gate is hit — so this eliminates the false `uncovered` at its root rather than merely diagnosing it.

CRT-2D7X.title: critic: a BLOCKING check is ungranted and unrunnable on one path

sections.Problem: `goals-1-3.md` makes `verify-coverage` a mandatory pre-review step and grades its output BLOCKING per missing file, but neither surface that would run it has the grant.
sections.Repro: Dispatch a coordinator review and have a `critic-reviewer` subagent attempt `prawduct-hook verify-coverage`.
sections.Actual: `critic-reviewer.md`'s `tools:` list — which, unlike a skill's `allowed-tools`, genuinely binds a dispatched subagent — carries **no `prawduct-hook` entry whatsoever**, so the coordinator path is **structurally blocked**. Verified still true at the tree.
sections.Expected: Either the command is granted on both paths, or the instruction is demoted and the BLOCKING check is removed from Goal 1 deliberately.
sections.Evidence: **Narrowed by observation hours after filing, and the narrowing matters**: a single-pass fork *did* run `verify-coverage` successfully despite its absence from `SKILL.md`'s `allowed-tools`, consistent with that file's own caveat that frontmatter enforcement is unreliable. So the fork path is **ungranted but not blocked**; only the subagent path is structurally blocked — and that is the path every `final`/`cumulative` review takes at scale. **A fix that only edits `SKILL.md` closes the half that was never broken.** This is a design call, not a typo: granting widens a surface deliberately restricted to no-execution (CRT-3X9D), and that argument must be made explicitly. **Second instance, so the fix wants the general form**: assert that every command an instruction surface mandates is present in the grant lists.

CRT-2P8V.title: critic: _GIT_REF_PREFIXES omits feat/, chore/, wip/, dependabot/

sections.Problem: The branch-name prefix set fixes the `missing-ref:` false positive for git-flow shops and silently leaves it for everyone else.
sections.Repro: A consumer product on `feat/`, `wip/` or `dependabot/` that backticks its own branch name in a build plan.
sections.Actual: The token parses as a file path, and `verify-chunk-refs` `missing-ref:` is **BLOCKING** in the Critic protocol — so the consumer gets a spurious blocking finding, the exact pain `171e630` removed for prawduct itself.
sections.Expected: Conventional-Commits prefixes (`feat/`, `chore/`, `refactor/`, `perf/`, `ci/`, `wip/`), bot branches (`dependabot/`, `renovate/`) and personal prefixes are all handled — or the enumerated set is replaced by a shape rule that does not require guessing a repo's conventions.
sections.Evidence: All safe under the existing extension rule — `feat/foo.py` keeps its extension and stays checked. The Check-7 three-products test makes the gap concrete: a web app on `feat/`, firmware on `wip/`, a CLI on `dependabot/` are all unhelped. BLD-3M7K already framed the general problem; this is the concrete, shippable follow-on to the fix that landed. **The release-scoped half is NOT filed here** — that is BLD-7K3Q, and filing it twice would split the fix.

CRT-2Q6D.title: critic: dangling docstring reference to a deleted gate function

sections.Problem: A docstring in `lib/critic_mode.py` names `_verify_resolutions_gate_check` as its mirror; that function was deleted in the kernel-v3 cutover and is asserted-absent by a stays-deleted pin.
sections.Repro: Read `lib/critic_mode.py` around the rule-1 comment (verified still present at `:254`).
sections.Actual: It points a reader at machinery that no longer exists.
sections.Expected: Repoint at the surviving mechanism — composed tree-keyed coverage via `coverage_algebra.coverage_verdict`, or `critic_consolidate._prior_review_fact` — or drop the mirror clause.
sections.Evidence: Pure documentation drift; no behavior depends on it. But it sits in the exact function CRT-8H3R will edit, so it is **cheapest to land as a rider on CRT-8H3R rather than standalone**. Found during the 2026-07-19 stale-branch salvage sweep, verified against develop rather than inferred.

CRT-3F7M.title: critic: a coordinator review can hang silently with zero partials

sections.Problem: `/prawduct:critic` runs `critic-begin`, writes a valid manifest, reports three reviewers dispatched, and returns — and no partial ever arrives, so `critic-consolidate` waits forever. The failure is **silent and indistinguishable from a slow review**, so an agent that waits patiently does the right thing and waits forever; worst case a builder gives up and proceeds unreviewed, bypassing the gate by timeout rather than by decision.
sections.Proposed change:
- **Run the repro, now that its blocker has cleared**: from the `context: fork` coordinator, dispatch the three reviewers with `run_in_background: false` and confirm the fork blocks until all three partials land, then consolidates in-turn
- Validate across a genuine 7–9 minute cumulative review, not a fast one
sections.Acceptance:
- [ ] Whether await-in-fork holds is answered empirically
- [ ] **The `_CACHE_WARM_INTERVAL_MINUTES = 4` constant is disposed of** — retired if the fork awaits, re-sized against the real TTL if it does not
sections.Scope-out: Re-measuring under the old confound. Candidate fix (b) already landed: the incomplete no-op renders a liveness verdict with a 15-minute grace window, so the hang is no longer silent.
sections.Evidence: **Every prior observation was taken with a confound present.** The `SubagentStop` matcher was `critic-reviewer` while the runtime `agent_type` is the scoped `prawduct:critic-reviewer`, and for `SubagentStop` Claude Code treats an alphanumeric matcher as a literal — so **the per-reviewer consolidation trigger had never fired on any install since it shipped** (fixed 2026-07-27). At least one "reviewers died with the fork" report was a misdiagnosis: they survived 7–9 minutes and completed while the parent inferred death at ~2.5 minutes and double-dispatched. **The field is routinely deviating from the documented dispatch-and-STOP protocol to get results, which means the sanctioned path is the defect** (Principle 16). **This item carries CRT-8Q6R's inherited `revisit:` clock** — the 4-minute interval was sized against an assumed 5-minute prompt-cache TTL; sessions run under a documented 1-hour TTL, so it is a constant known to be defending the wrong TTL. Changing it costs two edits by construction (constant plus guide), which is a deliberate guard, not a surprise.

CRT-3T6V.title: critic: two manually-verified CLI behaviors have no regression test

sections.Problem: Two behaviors in `bin/prawduct-hook` were verified by hand during discodon-upstream-defects and never pinned, so a regression that collapsed them would pass CI.
sections.Proposed change:
- Pin that `cmd_verify_chunk_refs` differentiates its `cannot-verify:` exit message from its `missing-ref:` exit message
- Pin `cmd_critic_begin`'s bare-repo sibling-worktree guard — the `.get('branch', '?')` fallback when a sibling worktree has no branch (detached or bare checkout)
sections.Acceptance: - [ ] Both surfaces have a pytest exercising the exact path
sections.Scope-out: Changing either behavior. Both are correct today; the gap is coverage.
sections.Evidence: Related: BLD-5J8N (the chunk-header parser family in the same command) and CRT-6W2N's Chunk 04 worktree-guard work.

CRT-3W6P.title: critic: refuse a full re-round when zero blocking findings remain

sections.Problem: Nothing detects an agent running round N+1 against an already-passing gate. Agents get trapped for 3–4 rounds reviewing the records the previous round wrote — the owner's words: *"this 'fixing records about records' has been prawduct's downfall in production."*
sections.Proposed change:
- **Round 2+ on the same chunk is `verify-resolutions` only**, enforced in `critic-begin` rather than in prose
- **Refuse a full re-round when zero blocking findings remain** — name the remedy instead of silently dispatching 4–10 minutes of reviewers
sections.Acceptance:
- [ ] A round that exists only because fixing generated it is refused, with an override that was designed rather than discovered
- [ ] A round justified by a genuine outside change still runs
sections.Scope-out: The prose half — it shipped. `building.md` now says warnings and notes **gate nothing** and are dispositioned; `critic-consolidate` emits the batch-fix directive on both paths, including the coordinator case where the fork returns no findings summary. **None of that is structural**, which is this item's whole thesis.
sections.Evidence: **Measured: four rounds, ~40 minutes, on a ~40-line change; zero blocking after round 1.** Reproduced independently in a consuming repo on a released version, where 100% of rounds 2–3's new findings were self-inflicted by the fixing. **Round 4 there is the sharpest design constraint this has acquired** — it was *not* waste (a merge brought ~4,300 lines into already-changed functions), so the refusal must discriminate fix-churn from a tree that genuinely changed for an outside reason. The discriminator is **what moved the tree between rounds**, not a round counter — and the evidence store already distinguishes these, since a fix-churn round's delta is exactly the files the previous findings named. **Every self-inflicted finding was one class: unverified factual claims in fix-time prose.** The learning-loop datum is the strongest argument for building it: the reporter had written the governing rule *hours before* committing two more instances of it. **Merged: CRT-8N5V**, the parent requirement, whose residual is entirely carried here plus the open question of whether `verify-resolutions` should review the delta at all — design them together.

CRT-4M2P.title: critic: nothing records which trigger consolidated a review

sections.Problem: Three call sites reach `consolidate()` with the same signature and none of them says who it is — the `SubagentStop` hook, the explicit CLI call, and the session-end backstop. There is no trigger field, and `consolidate()` takes no parameter that could carry one.
sections.Repro: Read the `review.critic` ledger event after any review and try to determine which path wrote it.
sections.Actual: The three paths are observationally identical: same evidence fact, same `.critic-findings.json`, same cleared marker, same ledger line.
sections.Expected: A `--trigger` field on the `review.critic` event, set explicitly by each call site.
sections.Evidence: **This is why CRT-2J8N was invisible for seventeen days** — a dead `SubagentStop` hook and a working one produce the same end state, because the other two paths silently cover for it. **It bit again the same day, in the review OF the fix**: a reviewer asserted the trigger "did consolidate here without an explicit call" in the same review whose warning 7 said nothing records which trigger fired. Those cannot both be true, and the claim is almost certainly false — the installed plugin still carried the bare matcher. **The real cost is VRF-002 being unverifiable as written**: "findings appeared and I did not type the command" is equally consistent with the backstop having done it. Do **not** infer the trigger inside `consolidate()` — the paths are indistinguishable from the inside. Sizing note: `ledger_append` parses a closed arg set, so this touches the parser and record builder too.

CRT-4V8P.title: critic: mode inference fires rule 4 on an unrelated build plan

sections.Problem: `infer-critic-mode` returns `chunk` for a clean working tree, because rule 4 fires on whatever `active_build_plan` points at — even a plan the branch has nothing to do with — and never checks that anything is reviewable.
sections.Repro: A standalone fix branch with all work committed, while `active_build_plan` points at an unrelated in-progress plan.
sections.Actual: Rule 4 returns `chunk`; `chunk`'s interval is empty; `critic-begin --mode chunk` correctly refuses with exit 1. A wasted round-trip, not a wrong review — the fail-closed refusal worked as designed.
sections.Expected: Inference checks for a non-empty interval before returning a working-tree-scoped mode, and rule 4 confirms the plan relates to the branch's changes.
sections.Evidence: **The same unbounded pointer misattributes review RECORDS, not just mode inference — this is the wider blast radius.** Observed twice more (2026-07-31, 2026-08-01) on branches with no plan of their own: the fork read `active_build_plan`, dispatched `--chunk 05 --scope <other>`, and **the manifest, the review fact and the ledger event were all attributed to an unrelated plan** while `record_lint` graded that plan's deliverables against this diff and returned zero findings — **a vacuous pass indistinguishable in the record from a real one**. The pointer was *not stale*, which is why "clear the pointer" is not the fix. `record_lint`'s `assumed` flag cannot help: it is set only when the dispatch carried **no** chunk. Scope: a records defect, not a review-quality one — reviewers read the diff, not the plan. GOV-3K7M is the narrow, cheap leg, not a replacement.

CRT-5H2D.title: critic: a blocking finding on a zero-length interval gates nothing

sections.Problem: A BLOCKING finding recorded on `base_tree == head_tree` is structurally invisible to every composition gate.
sections.Repro: Re-dispatch `verify-resolutions` against an unchanged tree, record a blocking finding, then run `check-cumulative-critic`.
sections.Actual: `satisfied … 0 unresolved blocking`. A real blocking finding existed, was correctly stored, and gated nothing.
sections.Expected: A blocking finding at any tree on the composed path produces `blocked`.
sections.Evidence: **Two independent doors, and a fix touching only one misses the other.** (1) `review_edges` ends with `if src == dst: continue`, so the fact is excluded from the graph **before either search phase runs** — including the phase whose entire job is to return `blocked`. The comment's premise ("contributes nothing a node doesn't") is true of *connectivity* and false of *findings*: the edge carries a payload the node does not. (2) `coverage_verdict` returns `covered` whenever `base_tree == target_tree`, **before** the edges are built at all. **Mint site**: `begin_review` refuses an empty diff except for `verify-resolutions`, deliberately — and nothing downstream validates `base_tree != head_tree`. **Severe rather than cosmetic**: this is the one failure mode kernel-v3 is supposed to make impossible — not a loud `uncovered` with a remedy, but `satisfied` while holding an unresolved blocker. The store is append-only and shared across worktrees, so already-recorded self-loop facts persist and only the composition-side fix makes them count.

CRT-5Q8W.title: critic: five skill-prose clarity fixes from the 2026-06-09 review

sections.Problem: A batch of small wording defects across the Critic and backlog skills, none changing behavior, all still live after the prose-diet pass.
sections.Proposed change:
- `review-protocol.md`: "Decide checks from signals below" is vague — make step 6 reference the Modes block's mode→goals mapping
- `review-cycle.md` Learnings Cross-Check: note that a later learning revoking or softening an earlier one **wins** (it currently assumes learnings are infallible)
- `framework-checks.md` Check 7: add a concrete avoid/prefer example for "strengthening the dynamic generation system"
- backlog SKILL `pick`: document the combined 2/2 = 1.0 effect of missing effort/impact defaults and drop the stale "(Q6)" label
- Decide PR-review evidence retention: archive to `.prawduct/.pr-reviews-archive/` or document why deletion is intended
sections.Acceptance: - [ ] All five sub-items are landed or explicitly dropped
sections.Scope-out: Sub-item (2) — the designer-handoff note — **resolved 2026-06-10** by the CRT-6F2N fix. Do not redo it.
sections.Evidence: Checked against the tree after prose-diet chunks 02–03: the diet compressed the surrounding text but **absorbed none** of these; all five still apply at slightly shifted locations. Sub-item (6) joined from PR-3J6W's residual, whose other three sub-items are verified resolved.

CRT-5Q8W.note: Five surviving sub-items across four different files; explicitly filed as a batch.

CRT-5W3P.title: critic: the two fastest-growing payload files carry no token budget

sections.Problem: `SKILL.md` and `review-cycle.md` grew +16.4% and +14.4% one commit after reviewer payload was ratified as a **P0 wall-clock lever**, and neither is in `LAST_MEASURED_TOKENS` or under a `test_token_budget` ceiling.
sections.Repro: Measure either file against the branch base; verified still absent from the table today (it holds only `building.md`, `review-protocol.md`, `goals-1-3.md`).
sections.Actual: The growth is invisible until someone measures by hand, which is how it was found.
sections.Expected: Both are budgeted, by the mechanism that already exists and already covers three files.
sections.Evidence: **They need different answers — do not fold them into one ceiling.** `SKILL.md` is on the payload path of **every** review, so a byte added there is paid by every dispatch: a straightforward budget case. `review-cycle.md` is **not** on the `chunk`-mode payload path — which is precisely why content was deliberately relocated into it — so its budget question is about *reader* cost and drift, not per-dispatch wall clock. A single shared ceiling would either over-constrain the relocation target or under-constrain the hot file. Record **token** figures, not the byte percentages above, which are a proxy.

CRT-6B9M.title: critic: add the guard-behind-a-closed-gate review heuristic

sections.Problem: A defense placed downstream of an unverified dispatch step provides zero coverage for that step's failure, yet reads as coverage in exactly the argument that should have questioned it.
sections.Proposed change:
- Record the heuristic as case-law in `learnings.md` first
- Then consider a clause in the review protocol under a coherence/soundness goal
sections.Acceptance: - [ ] The rule is written where a reviewer will meet it, with the discriminator stated as the **claim**, not the topology
sections.Scope-out: Leading with a protocol clause. Plenty of legitimate defense-in-depth is downstream of something and is not claimed to compensate for it, so a topology-based check would false-positive heavily.
sections.Evidence: **The instance**: `cmd_subagent_stop` early-returns unless `agent_type.endswith("critic-reviewer")` — a real, correct check. `operator-verification.md` VRF-002 cited exactly that defense as why matcher uncertainty was tolerable. But **the check sits downstream of the matcher**, the matcher never fired, so the guard never ran — and its presence is part of what made the uncertainty feel acceptable for seventeen days. **The tell is a sentence of the form "X is uncertain, but it's fine because Y handles it" where Y only executes if X succeeded.** Self-defeating, and detectable by reading — which is what makes it Critic-shaped rather than a test. Sibling shape: TST-9M2X's vacuous pin, the same family reached from the opposite direction. Case-law-first matches how the ephemeral-reference firewall shipped.

CRT-6D2N.title: critic: verify-resolutions refuses while unreviewed work is in the tree

sections.Problem: The anchor branch decides from a **commit-set** diff while the refusal guard tests a **tree** delta, and the two disagree in exactly the case that bites.
sections.Repro: Review a dirty working tree, commit that reviewed content verbatim, then do more judgeable work in the tree and run `critic-begin --mode verify-resolutions`.
sections.Actual: Exit 1, `nothing to verify: the prior review has no blocking/warning findings and nothing changed since` — while a 97-line unreviewed rewrite sat in the working tree. **The refusal reads as "everything is reviewed"; it actually means "everything I chose to look at is reviewed."**
sections.Expected: Intent is detected by **tree inequality** — prior `head_tree` != capture `head_tree` — not by the commit set.
sections.Evidence: Confirmed twice live, and the mechanism now matches the code as read. When the prior fact carries `head_commit: null`, `prior_commit` falls back to `dispatch_commit`, so a commit that merely **materializes the already-reviewed tree** makes `committed_since` non-empty and moves the anchor to committed HEAD — but the prior `head_tree` equals that commit's tree, so the delta computes **empty**. This is exactly the flow `review-cycle.md:70` documents as "a review of the dirty working tree vouches for the subsequent commit": **the vouching commit is what trips the detector.** Failure is silent in the direction that loses governance. Fix (a) and the non-misleading message (c) are compatible and probably both wanted.

CRT-6R3W.title: critic: sweep by the rule that generates a pattern, not the instances

sections.Problem: Instance enumeration is necessary but not sufficient. An agent ran exactly the tree-wide instance sweep and was **still short by four sites**, including two log lines one line below the ones it had just fixed.
sections.Proposed change:
- Route through discovery before any implementation — `stage: research` is deliberate
- Decide the actor question explicitly: reviewer states the generating rule; fixer must state the rule before claiming a sweep complete; or both, with the reviewer's rule as a hypothesis the fixer confirms or widens
sections.Acceptance: - [ ] A design pass that picks the actor on evidence, not inference
sections.Scope-out: Adding prose to one actor's protocol as the whole answer. The failure recurred **four times** under existing guidance, which is evidence that is the intervention most likely to fail again.
sections.Evidence: **The distinction to design against**: an *instance* is a string you can grep; a *rule* is a predicate over code that names the class. Grepping finds textual matches of what you already saw; applying the predicate finds sites that instantiate the class in forms you had not seen — which is exactly where the residue lives. What converged was articulating *"anything carrying request-body, path, or external-API text logs with %r"*, which surfaced two files no review round had named. **Cost signal**: each fix commit reopens the cumulative-Critic coverage gap and forces another delta review, so rule-vs-instance is a direct multiplier on review cost. **Merged: CRT-4X2N**, the enumeration half — the reviewer holds the pattern and can collapse N rounds into 1, and its two caveats bind here: make it CONDITIONAL on pattern-shaped findings, and require CLASSIFICATION rather than a dump, since most hits are legitimate (correction narratives quoting old wording, archived items, tests pinning old behavior).

CRT-7N4B.title: critic: a bare `clear --brief-only` bypasses the session guard

sections.Problem: The invocation-kind resolver classifies a bare `clear --brief-only` as CONTINUATION, and CONTINUATION neither sweeps the critic marker nor refuses — so adding one documented flag skips the CRT-3X9D guard.
sections.Repro: Issue `clear --brief-only` by hand, with no `--session-start`.
sections.Actual: Lands in CONTINUATION and passes the guard. **`--brief-only` is NEW in this bundle** — the flag, its classification and its usage-string advertisement all ship here for the first time, so this is a new surface rather than an inherited one.
sections.Expected: Either the CONTINUATION classification requires `--session-start`, or the exemption is made honest and pinned.
sections.Evidence: **The load-bearing invariant is NOT currently violated, which is why this is a warning** — verified: the marker sweep is gated on BOUNDARY/GUARDED, and both destructive halves are gated on `not brief_only`, so `.critic-active`, `.session-start`, `.session-base-tree`, `.session-reflected` and `.gates-waived` are all untouched. **What IS false is the justification**, and that is the actual defect: the docstring says a continuation *"mutates nothing"*, while the path demonstrably writes `.advisories.json` (asserted by this bundle's own test), regenerates the subagent briefing, and can run `git rm --cached` — mutating the git index. The correct qualified form already exists 29 lines below ("mutates no session state"), so the module disagrees with itself. **And the safe behaviour is incidental, not pinned**: the marker-present case for this argv shape has no test at all. Also: the shape is reachable **only** by hand, which is precisely the CRT-3X9D vector. Fix together with DOC-4T6P item (d).

CRT-8H3R.title: critic: require a review anchor to be an ancestor of HEAD

sections.Problem: Mode inference and `critic-begin`'s prior-fact anchor check only that an anchor SHA **resolves**, not that it is an ancestor of HEAD — so after a branch switch a sibling branch's record can latch a `verify-resolutions` dispatch onto a cross-branch delta.
sections.Repro: Work on branch B while SessionStart recorded branch A, with A's anchor still resolvable in the shared object store.
sections.Actual: A two-way diff spanning the divergence, full of phantom findings and a wasted review pass. `_commit_resolves` is just `git rev-parse --verify <sha>^{commit}`, which succeeds for **any** object including a sibling tip. Zero occurrences of `is-ancestor` anywhere under `lib/` or `bin/`.
sections.Expected: `git merge-base --is-ancestor <anchor> HEAD`, failing **closed** — exit 1 and any other failure both demote to cumulative/final.
sections.Evidence: **The soundness half is structurally gone; read the pre-v3 paragraphs as history.** kernel-v3 deleted `compute-verify-resolutions-scope` and `extends_cumulative`, and gates compose tree-keyed facts, so a sibling review can no longer spuriously satisfy `check-cumulative-critic` — pinned at `tests/test_cumulative_gate.py:412-417`. What survives is dispatch-side only, so the consequence is **proportionality and noise**, not gate soundness. **Port caveat**: the archived branch also patched `gates._compute_verify_resolutions_scope`, deleted in the cutover and asserted-absent by a stays-deleted pin — porting it breaks the pin; redirect that half to `critic_consolidate._prior_review_fact`. **Keep the test pattern**: both ported tests assert `_commit_resolves(...) is True` AND `_commit_is_ancestor(...) is False` before asserting the demote, so they prove the old guard would have passed. **Merged: CRT-6J4P** — read its folded body rather than assuming this fix closes it: CRT-6J4P is the *same-lineage* cross-bundle chain, where the anchor **is** an ancestor of HEAD, so an ancestor guard passes it and rule 1b still fires.

CRT-8L3Q.title: critic: the ledger anchor's overlap window needs a lock, not a probe

sections.Problem: `review_event_exists` is read-then-write with **no lock anywhere**, so two consolidations past the manifest-existence check can both probe before either appends.
sections.Repro: Two concurrent consolidations — made more reachable by v3.2.1 mandating concurrent coordinator reviewer dispatch.
sections.Actual: The window shrank from the whole consolidate body to the microseconds between probe and append. **Narrowed, not closed, and not "exactly once."** Verified: no `flock`/`fcntl`/`O_EXCL`/`os.rename`/`os.replace` in `critic_consolidate.py`, `evidence.py` or `ledger.py`.
sections.Expected: `consolidate` **CLAIMS** the manifest by atomic rename *before* doing work, making the probe a backstop rather than the whole guard.
sections.Evidence: The **REPLAY** path is completely closed by the probe; only OVERLAP remains. **Trigger for doing the work: a *second* surplus `review.*` event.** Today there is exactly one and it is nameable — `rev-20260729T233201Z-d91acd9e`, anchored twice a second apart — so the known one must stay distinguishable from a new one; count by **duplicated `fact_id`**, not by an events-vs-reviews subtraction, because ~140 pre-field events carry no `fact_id` at all. **Why it matters now**: `review-stats` is the instrument the record-mechanization success criterion reads, and `aggregate_review_stats` does not dedupe on `fact_id`, so a surplus anchor inflates the very measure review proportionality is judged on. This resurrects archived CRT-4B7X's original fix-shape — kernel-v3 made the store *fact* idempotent, which killed the store race but never supplied the lock.

CRT-9K2P.title: critic: a single-latest-fact view stands in for the evidence store

sections.Problem: The kernel-v3 rule is that gates compose over **facts**, never over a derived view. Three surfaces break that rule against the same single-slot `.critic-findings.json`, and one vocabulary gap sits on top of them.
sections.Repro: Record two review facts on one branch, disposition only the newer, then read the census, run `verify-resolutions`, and open the session handoff.
sections.Actual: (1) **Render**: `render-dispositions` composes over the newest fact only, so findings left undispositioned by an earlier review are invisible at exactly the surface a PR check reads, while the census reports clean — observed live, R-10..R-14 never dispositioned and three still unfixed at head. (2) **Write**: `_prior_review_fact` takes the cache's single `fact_id`, which always names the newest fact, so **every earlier fact for the same chunk is permanently undispositionable**. (3) **Read**: the session handoff summarizes the view instead of composing resolutions, so a fresh session confidently re-opens closed work. (4) **Vocabulary**: `verify-resolutions` scopes to blocking/warning and `disposition` offers only `--accept`/`--file`, so a note you actually **FIXED** must be recorded as ACCEPT — the census reads `accepted: 5` when the truth is `fixed: 5`.
sections.Expected: Compose over **every** review fact in the interval, and give a fixed note an honest kind.
sections.Evidence: **Read the objection before starting**: the corpus says fixing any one of these leaves the others standing. That is true of a *point* fix and is exactly the argument for treating them as one root — this item's own dedup note already names it ("both trace to a single-latest-fact view standing in for the store"). Scope caveat: no gate is presently wrong, because coverage composition reads the facts — what has no path to completion is the **disposition norm**, and the case to design against is the one *not* observed, a **blocking** finding stranded the same way. `stage: design` because the interval derivation must be decided, not because the direction is unclear. **Merged: CRT-2X7R, CRT-7P5J, CRT-3F7T.**

CRT-9T6M.title: critic: critic-begin has no guard against a concurrent dispatch

sections.Problem: `begin_review` unconditionally removes partials and overwrites the manifest, with no check for an existing manifest, an in-flight review id, or the critic-active marker.
sections.Repro: Two agents driving Critic runs in one session — not guarded anywhere.
sections.Actual: Partials already written are **deleted outright**; surviving reviewers write against the *second* manifest, so `files_reviewed`/`base_tree`/`head_tree`/`chunk` are attributed to the wrong interval; and the ledger event reads `--chunk` off whatever manifest is on disk, which is how the observed attribution loss happened.
sections.Expected: `begin_review` distinguishes stale from live — inside the in-flight grace window it refuses and names the remedy; past it, it clears as today.
