sections.Evidence: The reset is **deliberate** and its rationale is sound for the *stale* case and wrong for the *concurrent* one — and the code cannot tell them apart. **Reuse `_INFLIGHT_GRACE_MINUTES`** rather than inventing a second notion of "live". **A second, distinct collision path the manifest analysis does not cover**: `partial_path` is keyed by **role only, never by review id**, so two single-pass reviews in one worktree contend for one filename. Observed: fork B wrote `reviewer.json` against **A's** manifest and consolidated it; A's own write failed because the file existed. **The loser's only signal is a failed `Write`**, and nothing in the protocol says what that means — a fork reading it as terminal discards its findings silently, and in this instance A's finding was **BLOCKING**. The rendezvous wants a review-id-keyed path or an explicit refuse-and-name-the-remedy. Also: **the protocol should say how to wait for an in-flight review** — no guard helps a caller who never observes the marker.

CRT-R4Z2.title: critic: reviewers file meta-notes about other findings as findings

sections.Problem: A reviewer files an observation that is *about another finding* rather than an independent defect — a Learnings Cross-Check entry restating a finding, or a note restating another finding's consequence. This inflates the count and the disposition workload.
sections.Proposed change:
- Decide, in `review-protocol.md`, what a reviewer does when its observation is bookkeeping about, or a consequence of, another finding: fold it into that finding, file it at lower severity, or not file it at all
- Say how a reviewer *knows* — self-evident within one partial, but a cross-reviewer meta-note is written before the other partial is visible
sections.Acceptance: - [ ] The protocol states the rule and the recognition test
sections.Scope-out: **This is not a merge-key problem and does not touch `merge_findings`.** The two findings are genuinely different text about genuinely different subjects, so no similarity threshold should or does group them.
sections.Evidence: **The reporting half SHIPPED 2026-07-29**: `likely_duplicate_groups` (union-find over cross-goal findings, `DUPLICATE_SIMILARITY = 0.4` Jaccard, transitive) plus `distinct_finding_count`, a consolidate stdout note, a derived-view key, and 10 tests including a genuine regression anchor rather than a tautology. **Caveat: the derived-view key has no programmatic reader** — a test pins that it is always written, but nothing downstream consumes it. Three questions were decided with it: the judgment lives in deterministic code (kernel-v3 forbids a model in the fact write path); it is **advisory reporting, never a collapse or discard**, because a fuzzily-dropped real finding is invisible in merged output and strictly worse than over-counting; and it is two problems, of which only the first shipped. Observed: honest distinct count was ~13 of 16 notes.

CRT-7V4N.title: critic: shape-validate evidence-store tree SHAs before git argv

sections.Problem: Tree SHAs read back from evidence facts are passed to the git CLI without shape validation, so a corrupted or hand-edited fact could inject an arbitrary token into a subprocess argument vector.
sections.Proposed change:
- Validate each SHA at the read/compose boundary against `^([0-9a-f]{40}|[0-9a-f]{64})$`
- Treat a non-conforming SHA like any malformed fact: it **weakens coverage** (yields no edge), never crashes the gate
sections.Acceptance: - [ ] A malformed SHA in a fact produces no edge and no traceback
sections.Scope-out: Treating this as an active hole. argv is list-form with no shell, so the exposure is git **option injection** or confusing failures, not shell injection — this is hardening.
sections.Evidence: From the chunk-06 cumulative review of the kernel-evidence-store bundle. The regex tightens the review note's `{40,64}` range to the two real lengths, SHA-256-ready. Affected paths: `evidence.tree_diff` → `git diff` argv, and the gate paths feeding it.

CRT-4Q7K.title: critic: auto-detect API-exposing chunks the author did not declare

sections.Problem: The API versioning / error-model Goal-2 check fires only when a chunk author writes `**Exposed API:** <name>` in the build plan, so an author who forgets it gets no check.
sections.Proposed change: - Auto-detect API-exposing chunks from boundary-patterns globs or the surfaces a chunk actually touches, so an undeclared chunk still gets the check
sections.Acceptance: - [ ] A chunk that touches a declared contract surface is checked whether or not it declared one
sections.Scope-out: Replacing the opt-in trigger. This **hardens** the existing path against omission; it is an enhancement, not a gap in shipped coverage.
sections.Evidence: Idea-stage: needs a design pass on the detection signal (boundary-patterns globs vs diff inspection) and its false-positive posture before it is buildable. Deferred follow-up from the api-design feature, recorded in the concerns registry's Known Gaps. Note the dependency on BND-1S4K — an empty `boundary-patterns.md` gives a glob-based detector nothing to detect.

CRT-5M9J.title: critic: add a scope check that pressure-tests the requirement itself

sections.Problem: Every reviewer checks the work **as scoped** and never whether the requirement should exist or was ever built end-to-end.
sections.Proposed change: - Add one mandated question to the cumulative and PR protocols: does this capability trace to a documented requirement, and is it reachable and consumed end-to-end?
sections.Acceptance: - [ ] Both protocols carry the question
sections.Scope-out: Building machinery. **The fix costs a paragraph.**
sections.Evidence: The metallm blind spot, documented four times: scriob shipped 697 commits with an unversioned API on an unchallenged one-word deferral. TST-9M4X is the same reachability question asked one layer down, of the *test* that vouches for the capability.

DOC-4T6P.title: docs: five single-line documentation-accuracy defects

sections.Problem: Five documentation claims are false at the source, each independently verified, grouped because all five are single-line corrections.
sections.Proposed change:
- **(a)** `change-log.md:228` names `_has_build_plan_file` among four functions taking the project dir; three check out, that one takes `prawduct_dir`. The real fourth member is `_get_work_in_progress`. The same entry also records the `[DECISION]` reversing the change it claims
- **(b)** Three new prose pins landed under `tests/preferences/`; the Enforcement table gained rows for two. An unrostered pin is a rule enforced in CI that the product's **norm index** does not know exists
- **(c)** A concerns cell names a build plan that will be deleted — in the same table as the ephemeral-ref firewall row it violates. Restate the behaviour self-containedly
- **(d)** `cmd_clear`'s docstring keeps the "mutates nothing" quantifier its own change-log entry records as falsified; the correct qualified form already exists 29 lines below
- **(e)** A test comment asserts the clear hook is "excluded on compact"; it fires on compact now
sections.Acceptance: - [ ] All five corrected; (d) landed together with CRT-7N4B, which is its correctness face
sections.Scope-out: **Do NOT fix (e) by adding `tests/` to the prose pin's `SURFACES` roster** — verified by running the pin's own regex: widening the roster catches nothing here, including this defect, because it encodes a different proposition family. File-surface widening and claim-inventory widening are separate moves.
sections.Evidence: **THE INSTANCE IS ONE LINE; THE SEARCH-SPACE GAP IS THE DEFECT.** The sweep covered runtime strings and durable prose, and **test comments were never in the search space** — a test comment is durable prose a maintainer reads as license. The widened sweep was run so this states a result, not a suspicion: exactly one genuine stale claim across `tests/`. **Deeper cause**: this bundle reversed **two** propositions and only one was swept — enumerate the propositions a change reverses, then sweep each one's own formulations.

DOC-4T6P.note: Five independent documentation defects, (a) through (e). Grouped deliberately because each is a single-line correction, but they are five separable problems.

DOC-7J4M.title: docs: eight stale migration-scrub.md step references

sections.Problem: The runbook was renumbered 0–5 → 0–6. The single reference in shipped code is fixed; the rest sit in records and are stale.
sections.Proposed change: - **Name-anchor** all eight rather than renumbering them
sections.Acceptance: - [ ] The completion claim is a **query that returns empty** — e.g. `git ls-files | xargs grep -n "migration-scrub.*[Ss]tep [0-9]"` — **not** "I fixed eight"
sections.Scope-out: Renumbering. The eight in `refs:` are the sites known at filing, offered as a starting set and explicitly **not** the closure condition.
sections.Evidence: **The durable lesson, and why this is worth more than its effort suggests: "renumber them to match" would ALSO have been wrong.** Several stale references point at **`2c`**, and the runbook has **no lettered sub-steps at all** — so the obvious fix produces a *differently* wrong pointer that looks right, and the class regenerates at the next renumber. A step number is a claim about a document the citing work exists to change, so it is stale the moment the work starts. Note the recursion: BKL-2Q7F already learned this and re-anchored its refs from line numbers to step+op, and **those step-anchored refs are themselves now among the stale sites**. A count is unfalsifiable — it is true of any prefix of the real set.

DOC-7K4V.title: docs: api-contract.md omits the prawduct-hook backlog surface

sections.Problem: The backlog-service build plan declares `prawduct-hook backlog` an **Exposed API** — the marker whose whole purpose is to route the chunk through versioning and error-model review — and the product's own API contract artifact does not mention the surface at all.
sections.Repro: Read `.prawduct/artifacts/api-contract.md` looking for the op set, the envelope, the exit classes, or the compatibility promise.
sections.Actual: None of them are there. The artifact a reader is told is the API source of truth omits an API the product exposes.
sections.Expected: A section at the level the artifact uses for its other entries, stating the versioning and error-model position and **referencing** `documentation/backlog-service-api-contract.md` for operational detail.
sections.Evidence: The surface is not *undocumented* — `documentation/backlog-service-api-contract.md` and `skills/backlog/adapter-mode.md` both describe it in detail. The defect is that the two disagree **by omission** with no pointer between them, so a consumer asking "what does prawduct expose, and under what promise?" gets a confidently incomplete answer. Do not duplicate the detail — duplication is a second drift source. **Check in the same pass whether any other `**Exposed API:**` declaration is likewise missing from the artifact**; the gap suggests nothing links the declaration to the artifact.

DOC-8L3F.title: docs: CLAUDE.md exceeds the ~150-line instructions guidance

sections.Problem: CLAUDE.md is instructions, not documentation, and carries a ~150-line guidance the Critic warns above. It sits at 190 lines (re-measured 2026-08-01).
sections.Proposed change:
- Move architecture and reference content to `docs/` or `.prawduct/artifacts/`
- Compress redundant instruction
sections.Acceptance: - [ ] Project-specific content is back under the guidance, or the guidance is deliberately raised with a reason
sections.Scope-out: Cutting roster completeness to hit the number. A 2026-07-17 assessment added one necessary principle-roster line on exactly that reasoning — roster completeness beats the diet.
sections.Evidence: Overlaps MET-7R4J (cross-file rule interference); kept separate because that item targets redundancy across surfaces while this is the line-count budget itself. Run them together — MET-7R4J is the consolidation vehicle.

REL-3K9P.title: docs: the pruned-promotion runbook has no reachable verifier

sections.Problem: The runbook shipped with `last_verified: null` and named a **version** (v3.2.0's run) as its verifier — but whether the runbook opens at all is decided by the promotion's **shape**, so the trigger turns on a fact it never states.
sections.Repro: Read the runbook's trigger and try to determine whether it will fire.
sections.Actual: Nothing tells you. Phase 0 routes a whole-develop promotion down a path that never opens the pruned runbook, and a pruned one into it.
sections.Expected: The trigger is the **next pruned release, whenever one occurs** — a promotion shape, not a version number. Stamp `last_verified`/`verified_by` from that real execution.
sections.Evidence: **An overclaim was withdrawn 2026-07-29 and the withdrawal is worth keeping**: an earlier version asserted v3.2.0 is planned non-pruned and concluded the old trigger is "structurally unreachable". Both are unsupported — no release plan for v3.2.0 exists in the tree, and the owner's intent lived only in untracked handoff notes. The defect does not depend on the overclaim. **Nothing else tracked it**: REL-8P6M is archived, no advisory fires on `last_verified: null` (no code under `plugin/lib/` reads the field), and no open item referenced the runbook. **Scope — the publish half is what is unverified**: the candidate-tree build was rehearsed against the real v3.1.2 candidate and reproduced its three recorded conflicts, so effort is small.

REL-5W2J.title: docs: release-process.md omits three steps rediscovered every release

sections.Problem: Three release-prep steps are absent from the process doc and get rediscovered every release.
sections.Repro: Follow `docs/release-process.md` end to end.
sections.Actual: `pyproject.toml` carries a version and is stale at `3.0.3` — it missed v3.0.4, v3.0.5 and v3.1.0. `CHANGELOG.md` is what the version-delta banner actually reads and is named nowhere. `active_build_plan` is never cleared, so the shipped tree misdirects every session opening against it.
sections.Expected: All three are in the process doc.
sections.Evidence: All three were found by **deriving** `runbooks/cut-and-publish-a-plugin-release.md` from the runbook guide, not by reading the process doc — which is itself the signal. v3.1.1 patched the instances; the source stays wrong. The `CHANGELOG.md` half is REL-3M7K — cross-link rather than duplicate.

REL-7D4X.title: docs: the release change-log sweep selects the wrong set three ways

sections.Problem: Phase 1 says to find the topmost tag line carrying `release=` and flip everything *above* it. The selection is wrong in three independent dimensions.
sections.Repro: Derive the release-pending set by the runbook's stated method on any tree with out-of-order merges.
sections.Actual: **(1) Positional** — an entry that merged *below* the boundary but is genuinely unreleased is dropped silently; `release-plan-v3.1.1-hotfix.md` proves it. **(2) Scope-narrowed** — re-deriving with `grep scope=<the-one-you-remember>` returns a subset that looks complete: measured, 23 release-pending entries across six scopes, of which one scope was 7, so that grep missed 16 across five others. **(3) Pruned release** — the sweep appends `status=shipped` to everything above the boundary, marking **withheld** work as shipped; prawduct has pruned twice, so this is the pattern.
sections.Expected: Per-candidate: an entry is release-pending iff it carries no `release=` tag **and** its code is absent from the prior release's tree.
sections.Evidence: **Do not rewrite the rule yet — the hold survived its trigger firing.** The change-log-ledger decision was taken 2026-07-31: **GO on the design, HOLD on the schedule**, gated on which fleet migration is proven end-to-end first, backlog-to-Issues or change-log-to-ledger. Two unproven fleet paths must not be live at once. The stopgap — every release tags its shipping subset by hand across every scope — is re-bound from "until the decision" to **"until the ledger plan is scheduled and shipped"**, a longer and less certain window. **`stage: design` stays**: which shape survives (patch the sweep vs delete it with the ledger) is still open. Raise to `ready` when the ledger plan is scheduled, or if the ordering puts the ledger far enough behind that patching stops being throwaway. Carries REL-8P6M part (e) and its trigger.

REL-7D4X.note: Three independent selection defects that must be resolved together but are separable problems.

ENV-2W7K.title: environments: gitflow base, silent non-Python floor, --from-counts

sections.Problem: The framework assumes a repo-root Python project, a single checkout, and a main-based branch model — violated by engine subdirectories, .NET/Swift, worktrees, devcontainers and gitflow.
sections.Proposed change:
- Gitflow base detection that does **not** require knowing `base_branch:` exists
- The non-Python coverage floor goes **SILENT**, not noisy, for languages it cannot see
- Document `--from-counts` as the paved non-pytest path
sections.Acceptance:
- [ ] A gitflow repo gets the right base on its first PR without configuration
- [ ] A non-Python repo is not nagged by a floor that cannot inspect it
sections.Scope-out: **The worktree leg is DELIVERED — a future picker must not re-plan it.** A documented worktree workflow shipped (STH-4K7N Chunk 02, PR #107), plus the stop-path redirect signal and SessionStart worktree enumeration in `lib/briefing.py`.
sections.Evidence: **Attribution correction 2026-07-19**: the worktree-awareness leg was originally mis-credited to BRF-6K2D. What landed is the briefing's worktree enumeration; BRF-6K2D is the merge-awareness of the "delete the plan" nudge and remains fully open. Umbrella over COV-5H3N and STH-4K7N — dedup and `closes:` when planned. The owner's rule stands for any future worktree work: a short design note first, confirmed, before building.

ENV-2W7K.note: Explicitly an umbrella; its worktree leg already closed, leaving three unrelated legs.

ENV-7C4K.title: environments: a stale PATH prawduct-hook silently no-ops the data plane

sections.Problem: Inside a framework-repo worktree, bare `prawduct-hook` on PATH resolves to the **installed plugin cache** binary rather than the repo-local `bin/prawduct-hook`, and the version skew produces a silent no-op in the Critic data plane.
sections.Repro: Run a Critic review from a framework-repo worktree whose checkout is a newer lineage than the installed plugin.
sections.Actual: `critic-begin` ran the stale binary and **silently wrote no kernel-v3 manifest** — no error, no manifest, wrong-version semantics. The same bites a **second** data-plane write: the `SubagentStop`-triggered `critic-consolidate` also silently no-ops, leaving the review un-persisted until a repo-local call lands the fact.
sections.Expected: Either skills and docs inside the framework repo prefer the repo-local binary ahead of PATH, or the invoked binary compares its self-reported version against the repo's expected lineage and **refuses to proceed silently**.
sections.Evidence: **Any fix touching only `critic-begin` is incomplete** — it must cover the hook invocation path too, since the SubagentStop consolidate runs on the hook's own PATH. Dogfooding-specific: product repos legitimately run the plugin-cache binary; the skew bites only where the checkout is newer than the install. A silent no-op in the review data plane is the worst failure mode available here — **loud beats clever**.

GOV-3P8K.title: gates: deterministic tripwire for the ephemeral-ref firewall

sections.Problem: Ephemeral build identifiers — chunk numbers, build-plan and work-cycle names — leak into committed code comments and durable specs, where they dangle once the plan is deleted. Today only a Critic Goal-4 judgment check catches it.
sections.Proposed change: - A grep or hook check that scans committed comments and durable specs and flags leaks automatically, complementing the shipped Critic check
sections.Acceptance: - [ ] A real leak is flagged without flagging the blessed bookkeeping exemption
sections.Scope-out: **Building it now.** Deliberately deferred case-law-first — build only if the rule plus the Critic prove insufficient in practice, which is what the concerns registry already records.
sections.Evidence: **Design challenge is the false-positive posture**: "chunk" is an ordinary word (chunked data, memory chunk), and the bookkeeping exemption is real (change-log `chunks=`, backlog `closed-by:`, operator-verification). Any deterministic scanner has to separate a genuine leak from those. Idea-stage until that is designed.

STH-6D4Q.title: gates: tests_are_current fails open when .session-start is absent

sections.Problem: With no session marker the freshness gate accepts arbitrarily old passing evidence on nothing but a schema check, a zero failure count, and the presence of a timestamp.
sections.Repro: An unanchored working copy — no `.session-start` — with old passing evidence.
sections.Actual: `gates.py:156` returns True. The additive tree-validity clause sits **inside** the `if session_start:` branch, so on the no-marker path there is no tree check at all. The fail-open predates this bundle; what changed is that the old boundary reset used to write `.session-start` on its way through, so a `resume` **accidentally re-anchored** an unanchored worktree. That accidental repair is gone by design, so the path is now reachable indefinitely.
sections.Expected: Extend the tree-validity clause to cover the no-marker case — probably the cheapest sound option, since it answers "has anything judgeable changed" without needing a session clock.
sections.Evidence: **Read the second half's scoping before sizing work off it; an earlier draft over-generalized it.** Gating the `.session-reflected` unlink on `reflection_preserved` is a **net improvement, not a new hole**: the file survives a boundary **only when archival genuinely failed**, and that path prints an attributed NOTE naming the remedy. The residue at its true size: in the session *following* a failed archive, the blocking reflection gate can be satisfied by the previous session's text, because both readers check only presence and length. **Half three is the cheap half and is owed regardless**: the plan's own `[DECISION]` and Success #5 both assert freshness gates fail **closed**, which `gates.py:156` contradicts — a Living Documentation violation in a governing artifact, load-bearing because the DECISION's rationale rests on the false premise.

BLD-6P8T.title: governance: nothing verifies that intra-repo path references resolve

sections.Problem: `tests/test_plugin_packaging.py` pins where files may **live** and is blind to references pointing at paths that no longer exist.
sections.Repro: Relocate a source file and leave its readers untouched.
sections.Actual: The `plugin/` relocation shipped `bin/prawduct-hook` in five skills' instruction prose **and** in their `allowed-tools:` grants, with the full suite green throughout — because no test executes skill front-matter. The Critic caught it as BLOCKING.
sections.Expected: A test extracts repo-relative path-shaped tokens from the surfaces that fail silently — `allowed-tools:` grants, fenced and inline commands in skill and methodology prose, and `.prawduct/artifacts/**.md` — and asserts each resolves.
sections.Evidence: **Structural enforcement earned by a third recurrence.** `learnings.md:216` ("relocating a source file: sweep every READER of the old path") has now fired three times, which per the Learning Lifecycle promotes it from a rule to a mechanism. **Named risk**: a naive implementation drowns in false positives from prose that mentions paths illustratively — scoping extraction to **command position and front-matter** is what makes it high-signal, and `docs/norms.md` warns that a probe which misfires trains its reader to ignore the one real catch. The named-exception allowlist must be small and reasoned or the test becomes ceremony. Sibling: DOC-2R7M is the durable-artifact half.

BND-1S4K.title: governance: boundary-patterns.md is empty, so Goal 5 passes vacuously

sections.Problem: The Critic's Goal-5 contract-surface check is *instructed* to read `boundary-patterns.md` for the project's contract surfaces. Nobody has ever written one into it, so the check returns "no surfaces crossed" for the same reason on every change ever reviewed — and that answer is indistinguishable from the true one.
sections.Repro: Review a change that crosses two real contract surfaces and read the Goal-5 verdict.
sections.Actual: "No surfaces." The reviewer had to reconstruct the surface list from the code.
sections.Expected: The artifact carries the repo's real surfaces, and the `## Test Levels` table stops being the empty template.
sections.Evidence: **A second reader makes it worse in products than here, and the two legs point opposite ways.** `lib/risk.py::_boundary_pattern_paths` scrapes backticked paths from the same artifact into `resolve_surfaces`, which escalates a change to the three-reviewer roster. Where **no** `risk_surfaces:` key is declared — the fleet default — an empty artifact means review depth silently falls back to the file-count rule on exactly the contract-crossing changes that should escalate. **This repo declares `risk_surfaces:`, and a declared key is exclusive**, so filling the artifact here fixes Goal 5 and changes the risk tier not at all, while filling it in a product that declared nothing **raises** that product's review depth. **Already done, so the sweep does not redo it**: a header stating that the artifact is partially filled and its silence is not evidence of absence, plus two real surfaces with the evidence that proved them real. **The scoping question lands here and nothing prejudges it**: evidence-driven accretion versus one inventory pass. The case against inventory (an inventoried list of plausible surfaces is how a document becomes decoration) is an argument to weigh, not a constraint already imposed. **Not a duplicate of SCN-8T4R or GOV-5N8R** — those are two instances each bundled with its own guardrail; fixing all three one at a time would still leave the check vacuous in a repo with no instances filed.

GOV-2R8K.title: governance: sweep duplicated facts to one home plus references

sections.Problem: A fact — a number, a behaviour claim, a path, a rule statement, a schema — should have one home closest to the mechanism that owns it, with every other mention a reference. If changing a fact requires editing N places, N−1 are already wrong.
sections.Proposed change:
- Complete the enumeration first; it is the first acceptance criterion and the list below is a starting set, not the set
- Migrate each duplicated fact to one home plus references
sections.Acceptance: - [ ] The four existing single-purpose mechanisms end up as **references to the general norm** rather than four independent inventions of it, or the sweep reproduces the defect at the level of the rule itself
sections.Scope-out: Assuming a lint is owed. The Enforcement row is **Critic-judgment-only** — "is this a second authoritative statement or a reference?" has no reliable mechanical hook for prose, and a lint that guessed would flag every legitimate quotation. Specific fact *classes* are mechanizable and `suite-total-claim` already is.
sections.Evidence: **Tracking ref for a `## Direction` norm born 2026-07-31, `Status: in-transition`. Measured why now**: on one cumulative review **9 of 23 findings were one fact copied and drifting** — not design problems, duplication — and the repair applied to the largest was itself wrong, restoring agreement while preserving the duplication that will break it again. **The reframe is the point**: the coherence question becomes *"why are there two?"* rather than *"do these agree?"*, and the fix becomes *delete one*. **A KIND the enumeration does not yet contain**: every listed duplication is a copied *claim* that a grep for the sentence finds; LRN-7H3D is a copied **derivation** — no shared string, three consumers independently computing one predicate — and a prose sweep walks straight past it. Say explicitly whether derivations are in scope.

GOV-2W7Q.title: governance: operator-verification.md is a write-only queue

sections.Problem: Work is deferred *into* the queue correctly and conscientiously — the entries are detailed and well-written — and then never comes back out. Six of eight entries are pending, the oldest for seventeen days.
sections.Proposed change:
- Write a **drain plan** — verify, accept-with-rationale, or re-scope each pending entry — sequenced **ahead of** flipping `operator_verification_required`
- Decide the question the flag actually poses today
sections.Acceptance:
- [ ] Each pending entry has a disposition
- [ ] The **split-the-deferral rule** is written where deferral decisions are made
sections.Scope-out: **Just flipping the flag.** It would immediately block the next PR on six pending entries, several needing a live harness or an unrun migration.
sections.Evidence: **This is the escape analysis for CRT-2J8N and it outranks the bug it explains.** VRF-002 was filed 2026-07-10 to verify exactly that defect, and its own final step names the suspect matcher string — **seventeen days** before an unrelated review found it. The system that was supposed to catch this did catch it, on paper, and then never ran. **The stated reason the gate is off no longer describes what the queue holds**: the comment justifies the default by prawduct having no visual surface, but the entries are **live-harness integration checks** — does a hook fire, does a matcher match, does a CLI round-trip against a real repo. **The generalizable half**: VRF-002 deferred all three of its facts on the grounds that matcher semantics vary by version — true of the delivery facts, **false of the static half**, which was testable that day and was broken. When deferring, split *"can this be true in principle"* (static, testable now) from *"does the harness actually do it"* (live) — **only the second belongs in the queue.**

GOV-3D6X.title: governance: VRF-010's closure did not propagate to three surfaces

sections.Problem: VRF-010 verified all three relationship and timeline readers live and discharged MIG-3. That closure never reached the surfaces that still encode the pre-verification state.
sections.Repro: Read `project-state.yaml`'s `integration_test_strategy` and the Chunk 09 gate list.
sections.Actual: `project-state.yaml` still says the shapes are "fake-verified only until those run — tracked as BKL-3N8Q", and **BKL-3N8Q is now archived shipped**, so the citation resolves to a closed item. Chunk 09's list does not contain the flips it owes.
sections.Expected: Chunk 09's list carries the flips, the `project-state.yaml` claim is corrected, and VRF-010 is recorded as discharge evidence in the relevant bodies.
sections.Evidence: **This is about the flip LIST being complete, not about flipping now** — the release convention holds and nothing should be marked shipped ahead of Chunk 09. The risk is the same deferral-cascade failure this branch already hit once: a chunk's membership changing while the sections that compute against it are not opened. Note `project-state.yaml` cites BKL-3N8Q **by id** under an explicit do-not-renumber instruction, so the propagation updates the surrounding claim rather than the id. Per D4, a `status=shipped` call stays explicit and human-made, never inferred from an audit — recording evidence is not a status change.

GOV-3K7M.title: governance: record_lint never sees the manifest's scope

sections.Problem: `critic_consolidate.begin_review` calls `record_lint.lint_records_safe` without `scope`, though `scope` is a **live local in that same function** and is written into the manifest eighteen lines later. The chunk id comes from the dispatch and the plan comes from `active_build_plan`, and nothing checks they agree.
sections.Repro: Review a branch whose scope-named plan differs from `active_build_plan`.
sections.Actual: **The first true positive this has cost, not another vacuous pass.** The deliverable check graded the *pointer's* plan while the *reviewed* plan cited a deliverable path **four times** that did not exist. `chunk-ref-missing` reported **0** — the check that exists to catch "a declared deliverable that isn't there" reported clean on a diff where four of them weren't.
sections.Expected: Thread `scope` into `lint_records`/`lint_records_safe` and prefer the scope-named plan over the pointer. When the two **disagree**, that is the `unchecked` case, not a silent grade of whichever won — and an unrunnable check must say so **in its counters**, never print four zeros that read identically to a clean check.
sections.Evidence: **The fix belongs in the check, not the pointer.** `active_build_plan` was **correct** — the other plan is legitimately in progress, which is what the pointer means; clearing or re-pointing it would be wrong. The dispatch already knew which plan was under review and the manifest already records it. `_check_chunk_refs`'s `assumed` flag cannot help: it is set only when the dispatch carried **no** chunk. **Merged: GOV-2H6X**, the reporting ask — five consecutive reviews stated the same `unchecked:` caveat and those zeros were quoted as "0 findings" in durable records by readers who did not read the line above them. Both asks land in one change; CRT-4V8P still owns mode inference and attribution, which a record-lint argument does not reach.

GOV-3M9T.title: governance: the reconciled-files norm amendment did not cascade

sections.Problem: `architecture.md` was amended to name `CLAUDE.md` in the reconciled-files carve-out. Two sibling artifacts restate the same enumeration and neither was updated — and **both were edited in the same bundle**, so this is a missed cascade rather than an untouched file.
sections.Repro: Read `security-model.md` and `api-contract.md`'s enumerations of the plugin's write authority.
sections.Actual: Three governing artifacts describe that authority and two describe an authority the installer demonstrably exceeds — so a reader who reaches `security-model.md` first concludes the plugin violates its own least-authority norm by anchoring `CLAUDE.md`.
sections.Expected: Both enumerations restated to match, **with the falsifying grep carried alongside** so a fourth copy cannot hide.
sections.Evidence: The amendment's reasoning was that the enumeration was **incomplete at ratification** rather than permissive-by-omission — `init_product.py` has created-or-anchored `CLAUDE.md` and `migrate_plugin.py` has edited it in place since before the norm was written. This is the exact class the repo already has a learning for (*a recorded scope narrowing is a CASCADE, not an annotation*) and the exact shape of GOV-4B9N, where a ratified amendment sat in one artifact while another kept the pre-amendment form.

GOV-4D2Y.title: governance: the descent-obligation marker reaches only new onboards

sections.Problem: `/prawduct:learnings` points every product at a `prawduct:descent-obligation` marker that only newly-scaffolded products receive, because `init_product.py` guards the starter write with `if not learnings.is_file()`. **The defect is closed for the empty set and open for the real one** — the live fleet is entirely already-onboarded.
sections.Repro: Open `.prawduct/learnings.md` in any repo onboarded before 2026-08-01 and look for the marker.
sections.Actual: No marker. The shipped skill instruction points at a header section that does not exist, and nothing — not onboard, not migrate, not a re-run — ever backfills it.
sections.Expected: A `/prawduct:doctor` health check detects a preamble with no marker, reports **degraded**, and offers to insert the obligation **above the first rule**.
sections.Evidence: Verified: `grep -rn "descent-obligation" plugin/ tests/` returns exactly three sites — the starter constant, the reader that points at it, and a position guard test. **No detector, no repair, no advisory anywhere between the writer and the reader.** **Why this survived review**: prawduct's own `learnings.md` carries the marker, hand-added years before `init_product` existed, so every check performed from inside prawduct comes back green — the same blind-spot class as GOV-6X2N. **Position is load-bearing, not cosmetic**: the guard pins that a reader meets the obligation *before* the rules it governs, so an append-to-end repair satisfies a naive presence check and is still wrong. Two open questions: whether this extends health check #5, and whether the inserted prose comes from a shared constant (GOV-2R8K argues it must).

GOV-4M7K.title: governance: coverage-status layer 0 disagrees with the ambient nudge

sections.Problem: `cmd_coverage_status` computes layer-0-active purely from "not `structural_characteristics_recorded`", without the product-work gate the ambient layer-0 briefing nudge applies.
sections.Repro: A freshly-onboarded empty repo — no code, no `docs/` — then run the doctor coverage-status report.
sections.Actual: The report says layer 0 is active and coverage is degraded, while the ambient session-briefing advisory correctly stays **silent** and doctor Health Check #6 also gates on product work. The report is more eager than the nudge it claims to mirror.
sections.Expected: Gate the layer-0 determination on `_has_product_definition_work` too, so the report and the nudge agree on a fresh repo.
sections.Evidence: Bounded and cosmetic — a report line, no wrong behavior. Filed as a Critic NOTE from the structural-coverage cumulative (R-2). The report's own claim is that it "reads the SAME expectation table", which is what makes the divergence worth correcting rather than documenting.

GOV-4T9P.title: governance: migrate binding-method prescriptions to advisory phrasing

sections.Problem: A governing artifact says what must be true and how it will be checked, and those bind. Where it also prescribes *how* — a chunk's `Deliverables`, a named call site, a skill's step ordering — that is the author's best guess made before the code was read, and text that asserts method as **binding** leaves a reader unable to tell advice from authority.
sections.Proposed change:
- Complete the enumeration first; the confirmed sites are `plugin/templates/build-plan.md` (where `Deliverables:` is phrased as a contract, and it is the phrasing authors copy) and `plugin/methodology/planning.md` (which teaches that phrasing)
- Migrate the phrasing that propagates
sections.Acceptance: - [ ] A builder who finds a better route takes it and records why, without reading it as a departure
sections.Scope-out: **Explicitly NOT violations, and a later reader must not relax them**: `building.md`'s read-this-first instruction (knowledge delivery, not method); every `## Direction` invariant in `architecture.md`; the Critic and PR gates; the commit and merge conventions in `CLAUDE.md`. **Verification structure binds unchanged** — independent review, mutation-proof, mechanical enumeration — because it constrains the output contract rather than the route.
sections.Evidence: **Tracking ref for a `## Direction` norm born 2026-07-31, `in-transition`. Measured**: three chunk-level prescriptions were wrong on one branch — an inert delivery site, a test file that does not exist, and a decorative deliverable naming dead code — while **every goal-level statement held**. The converse held too, which is why the carve-out exists: mutation-proving caught two tests the builder was confident about, and `governed-by-gap` found 22 gaps across 8 plans. **Two precision notes so the sweep does not mis-grep**: `planning.md` contains **no literal `Deliverables:` string** — it teaches the concept — so a field-name grep wrongly concludes it is clean; and in the template the field appears only inside worked examples, so **the example *is* the spec**. Neither file was itself wrong. Enforcement is Critic-judgment-only by design.

GOV-4X9M.title: governance: treat strategy-artifact backfill as retroactive discovery

sections.Problem: Authoring a strategy artifact is a solo agent task, so it tends to codify current practice as if it were intended design, and it cannot know the owner's intent — which lives in the owner's head, not the repo. **The Critic currently rewards the failure mode**: a cumulative review praised prawduct's own artifacts for being "accurate to prawduct's actual system", and accuracy-to-current-code is the wrong success metric for a document meant to lead development.
sections.Proposed change:
- Reuse the existing discovery flow as an **interview**, rather than building a second one
- **Elicit the mode, don't presume it**: draft-from-what-is-built vs first-principles; capture-current-state vs set-direction
- A just-in-time, **stakes-calibrated** nudge when requested work would benefit from a missing artifact (security-model before auth is gold; observability before a copy tweak is noise)
- Layered opt-outs: decline-once (relevance-triggered re-surface, never calendar), decline-this-doc (a recorded `(not relevant — X)` stub), decline-everything (a scoped preferences posture)
- A Critic objective flip: a purely-descriptive artifact that rubber-stamps current behavior is a **finding**
sections.Acceptance:
- [ ] Backfilled artifacts state **intended design** and flag divergences from code as explicit owner decisions
- [ ] Opt-outs are **validated against recorded characteristics** — a `(not relevant)` security stub on a product with `handles_sensitive_data` is a detectable contradiction
sections.Scope-out: State-2 stale-doc detection; forcing anything (advisories only advise); a second discovery flow; designing the advisory tuning.
sections.Evidence: **Divergence splits into two gaps with OPPOSITE handling.** **Type 1 — code below norm**: the documented goal is genuinely best practice and the code lags; approval means ratify plus backlog the alignment. **Type 2 — norm below best practice**: the owner wants to enshrine a sub-optimal practice *as* the norm; approval is the **opposite** of accept. This punctures the earlier claim that owner ratification *is* the definition of best practice. **But the agent has NO VETO** (corrected): every best practice is a defeasible heuristic and the developer holds context the agent cannot see, so the terminus is **always ratify** — surface the practice and its reasoning, **elicit the why** (which often reveals the "wrong" practice is right here), then record honestly. **The only thing the agent ever declines is to LAUNDER.** The three dispositions map onto norms.md's Migrate / Grandfather / Contain.

GOV-4X9M.note: A large design spanning the interview flow, the nudge, the opt-out ladder and the Type-1/Type-2 divergence model.

GOV-5H2Q.title: governance: require a per-principle disposition map in build plans

sections.Problem: The 24 principles are stored guidance, and "consider the principles" is unverifiable and self-certifying — a reader can believe they considered them and leave no residue either way. Principles end up shaping *prose about* the work more than the work.
sections.Proposed change: - Extend `governed_by:` to accept `artifact: principles`, so the existing `governed-by-gap` lint requires 24 dispositions
sections.Acceptance:
- [ ] **"No bearing" is cheap and legal — one word.** Most rows will be that, and forcing every row to claim applicability is how the map becomes wallpaper
- [ ] **A bearing row carries a CITATION or a CONSEQUENCE.** A bare "Principle 11 — conforms" is unfalsifiable and did no work; the test of a good cell is that a reviewer can disagree with it
- [ ] **A ratio tripwire**: a map where all 24 bear, or none do, is flagged suspect
sections.Scope-out: Folding this into the learnings-firing plan, whose Out of Scope explicitly forbids changing what the Critic reviews or how gates compose. Filed separately so that plan's scope stays honest.
sections.Evidence: **The insight is that requiring an OUTPUT beats requiring an INPUT** — you cannot write the cell without inspecting the decision. Cheap because prawduct already runs the mechanism: `governed_by:` carries one-line dispositions per norm, `record_lint._check_governed_by` counts each artifact's `## Direction` norms and fires on under-disposition, and `planning.md` already ratifies the idea in prose. **Scale caveat to design against**: a typical plan disposes 7–12 *repo-specific* norms, so most genuinely bear; 24 *universal* principles is a different regime where most will not.

GOV-5N8R.title: governance: a standardized id pattern keeps acquiring narrow copies

sections.Problem: A sweep that repairs N sites leaves nothing that prevents site N+1.
sections.Proposed change: - Give the id pattern **a single definition plus a guardrail**, not another sweep — which is exactly what `boundary-patterns.md` exists to carry
sections.Acceptance: - [ ] One definition, one pin, and a recorded boundary-patterns entry
sections.Scope-out: **The local one-line widening of the spike's regex.** It rides with the next branch that touches those spikes and is **not** what this item asks for.
sections.Evidence: BKL-4W7H widened the backlog id shape in four places and is annotated BUILT 2026-07-28. Yet `tests/spikes/backlog_archive_value.py:52` defines its own `ID_RE` with a fixed 4-char suffix and a single hyphen — a **fifth** narrow copy, written **days after** the sweep, and it cannot see `MIG-M4-REMOVE`. **Related, not duplicate**: CRT-6R3W is the *reviewer-behavior* statement of this class, and SCN-8T4R is a sibling instance; neither would close this.

GOV-5R8T.title: governance: a concerns row claims methodology coverage never written

sections.Problem: `cross-cutting-concerns.md:42` claims pipeline coverage for the "backend declaration before a governance read" concern at two stages, attributing text to `discovery.md` and `building.md`.
sections.Repro: Search either file for the attributed text, then `git log -S` over the phrasing.
sections.Actual: Neither file contains it, and **no commit ever added it** — this is not drift from a deleted rule, it is coverage recorded without ever being written.
sections.Expected: The row states what is actually true, and the remaining rows are swept for the same defect.
sections.Evidence: **Why it matters more than a stale cell**: the registry is what a reviewer consults to decide whether a concern is *already handled upstream*. A row asserting Discovery + Builder coverage reads as "two stages catch this before it reaches me", so the one stage that genuinely could — Critic judgment — is the only real coverage while the matrix reports three. **Recurrence, not a one-off**: BLD-4Q8W is the identical failure on row :36. Two rows, same mechanism, and a hand-maintained matrix has no mechanism that would have caught either — which is why the fix is two-part: correct the row, then sweep the rest.

GOV-6D4Q.title: governance: a deletion-only simplification pass over the surface

sections.Problem: Governance work generates findings, findings become items, items become governance work. Over 26 days the open backlog went **50 → 169** (3.38x) while enforcement Python went ~15,500 → ~27,400 LOC. The review that was supposed to shrink the surface is one of the things that grew it.
sections.Proposed change: - Produce a **delete/keep list against existing surface** and nothing else
sections.Acceptance:
- [ ] **This pass may not file new backlog items.** The constraint IS the design
- [ ] The 12 still-open Wave 2/3 items from the 2026-07-02 review are each dispositioned
- [ ] The four change-log deferrals that cited a review which did not exist get an explicit disposition rather than continued inheritance of a bad reason
sections.Scope-out: **A conventional audit is explicitly rejected.** The 2026-07-02 review was a seven-agent sweep whose diagnosis was correct and owner-accepted, and the surface grew 3.4x anyway; another sweep is predicted to file another twenty items. **The diagnosis is already in hand; what is missing is a deletion decision.** Treat "we should audit this properly first" as the failure mode this item exists to refuse.
sections.Evidence: **Work was deferred against a review that did not exist** — a repo-wide grep for "simplification review" returns one change-log line and nothing else. **Waves 2 and 3 have not been picked once in 26 days, and that non-pickup is evidence, not a scheduling accident.** **This item is itself an instance of what it forbids** — filing it moved the count 169 → 170, and the body's figures are left reading 169 deliberately; the pass should count itself among the deletion candidates. **Known tension, recorded not resolved**: the backlog service is the largest new governed surface prawduct has added, so migrating relocates some tax as much as it reduces it — treat the service as in-scope for deletion review like anything else, not exempt because it is new. Sequenced **after** Chunk 06 and **before** Chunks 07 and 08.

GOV-6N4W.title: governance: detect norm-birth phrasing at prompt time

sections.Problem: "We should always X", "from now on Y", "never Z again" is norm birth, and today it is captured only if someone notices. A norm born ambient rather than recorded has no lifecycle.
sections.Proposed change: - A UserPromptSubmit classifier that detects norm-shaped phrasing and nudges capture into the norm registry
sections.Acceptance: - [ ] The detector clears the precision bar WMK-4Q9T set, before it ships
sections.Scope-out: Building it now. Deferred for precision risk: the work-model prompt-term tripwire shows prompt-time classifiers misfire on ordinary prose and desensitize the very nudge they power.
sections.Evidence: Needs a design pass on the detection signal (phrase patterns vs heavier classification), its false-positive posture, and **usage evidence from shipped v1 norm capture** — advisory probes, janitor Norm Health, doctor ratification — showing prompt-time detection adds value over capture-at-reflection.

GOV-6X2N.title: governance: the green-is-evidence directive is dark off Python

sections.Problem: `_GREEN_IS_EVIDENCE_DIRECTIVE` fires off `changes_referenced`, which is populated by `bin/test-reference-verify`, which **skips every non-Python file**.
sections.Repro: Any Swift / Go / TS / Rust / C# product.
sections.Actual: The set is empty, the trigger never fires, and the directive is silently dark — in a product whose owner has no way to observe that it was supposed to fire.
sections.Expected: The directive triggers off a language-agnostic signal — the changed-file set, or test-evidence presence.
sections.Evidence: **Why this matters more than one dormant directive**: per LRN-2D7Q, code-delivered directives are the **only proven path** by which prawduct ships a general learning into a consuming product, so if one of the two exemplars only works on Python repos, the proven path is narrower than the item citing it assumes. **Filed rather than folded into COV-4M2J**: same root cause, different consequence, and plausibly a different fix — this could close by re-triggering off a language-agnostic signal with **no** language-aware coverage floor in existence, and should not wait on an L-sized requirements pass it does not depend on. **The cheap half is worth doing regardless: name the item.** The code comment says the limitation is "tracked separately" and names nothing — a tracking reference pointing at no id is not a tracking reference. LNG-5W8R would make the dormancy **visible** but not make it **fire**.

GOV-7W3D.title: governance: 6 of 10 Direction norms carry no disposition

sections.Problem: The plan's `governed_by:` frontmatter records one disposition for `security-model` (3 norms), two for `architecture` (4 norms — and one quotes a *sub-clause* rather than a norm), and one for `api-contract` (3 norms). Applicability for the remaining six was **assumed, not recorded**, and silence reads as `conforms`.
sections.Repro: Count each cited artifact's `## Direction` norms against its dispositions.
sections.Actual: Six undispositioned, three of them directly implicated by the bundle. `observability-strategy.md` carries **three ratified norms with plain jurisdiction** and is absent from `governed_by:` **entirely**.
sections.Expected: A disposition **per norm** — `conforms` / `ruling needed` / `exception` / `amendment proposed` / `inapplicable because X` — plus `observability-strategy.md` added.
sections.Evidence: **Deadline is literally "before Chunk 06 runs".** **One norm of ten is settled and the rest stands.** The `--apply`/dry-run norm was **amended, not weakened**, by owner ruling: approval binds at the **operation** level (one informed confirmation naming blast radius and irreversibility, before the first write), with granular steps inside an approved operation proceeding without re-confirmation. **The old form was doubly broken, and that is the reusable part**: (1) *unsatisfiable* — the adapter implements no generic `--apply` contract, so shipped code already departed with no recorded decision, and a norm live code silently violates is a claim, not governance; (2) *wrong to satisfy literally* — gating ~900 migration writes on per-action confirmation **manufactures the rubber-stamping the norm exists to prevent**. **Merged: GOV-8C3W**, whose class half is already shipped as `record_lint`'s `governed-by-gap` (yield: 22 gaps across 8 plans); its residual is the four-line `security-model` sweep, which is a subset of this.

GOV-8R3F.title: governance: port the doctor surface-by-exception taxonomy to janitor

sections.Problem: The janitor's Step-3 Reconcile still presents candidates as a flat single confirm-or-correct block, which at scale becomes a wall of text the owner skims and rubber-stamps — the "blanket 'looks good' that never engages the forks" failure ratification exists to prevent.
sections.Proposed change: - **Reuse the shipped doctor taxonomy — do not design a competing one.** Apply the clear-to-ratify / needs-a-ruling split, foreground only candidates needing a decision, collapse the clearly-safe ones into a bulk confirm-in-summary, and honor the ~6-item flat-dump ban
sections.Acceptance: - [ ] Surface-by-exception **never silently ratifies** the un-surfaced candidates — the collapsed set still gets an explicit bulk confirm with a visible count
sections.Scope-out: A fresh design. Exception criterion, surfacing shape and bulk-confirm guard are all already designed and proven in the doctor precedent; this is a port.
sections.Evidence: The doctor Norm Ratification Flow shipped exactly this fix; the janitor sibling carries the identical failure mode. Auto-binding a norm the owner did not engage is a norm-birth decision made by default, which `docs/norms.md` § No auto-ratification forbids. `stage: ready` because the precedent removes the open design question.

REL-4Q9V.title: release: hard-remove status=merged and the stamp-merged machinery

sections.Problem: The change-log lifecycle carries retired vocabulary: `merged` in `VALID_STATUS_VALUES`, and `stamp_merged`/`cmd_stamp_merged` which are deprecated-but-callable with a stderr notice.
sections.Proposed change:
- Drop `merged` from `VALID_STATUS_VALUES`
- Delete `stamp_merged` and `cmd_stamp_merged`
- Consolidate to one scope identifier
sections.Acceptance: - [ ] No caller and no vocabulary entry survives
sections.Scope-out: **Deferred to a future major** — this is a breaking vocabulary change, and fail-loud validation already removed the P0 urgency.
sections.Evidence: **The lifecycle half shipped 2026-07-10.** Statusless-until-release is now documented and code-supported: `collect_release_pending_scopes` enumerates statusless tagged scopes, the merge-flow stamp step is **removed** (so the original cascade list is already shorter), create-flow Step 1d establishes that the PR carries its own bookkeeping, and `docs/release-process.md` plus the template are rewritten. A deletion-over-patching candidate.

CRT-7Q2T.title: critic: the no-test-execution rule does not bind dispatched subagents

sections.Problem: The Critic's no-execution guarantee rests on a pure-allow `allowed-tools` list, which does not bind Agent-dispatched subagents.
sections.Repro: A coordinator-pattern review on a diff with affected test files.
sections.Actual: A subagent ran the affected test files directly — 217 passed, reported in the review summary — despite the SKILL prose instruction and the tool list. The review conclusion was unaffected, but the boundary exists so reviews cannot mutate or depend on session state.
sections.Expected: The constraint binds structurally: extend the critic-active marker enforcement to test and build execution, or have the coordinator pass an enforced `allowed-tools` to Agent dispatches.
sections.Evidence: **Same gap class as CRT-3X9D**, whose marker guards only `prawduct-hook clear` — one mutation site, and everything else relies on prose. Note that `critic-reviewer.md`'s `tools:` list **does** genuinely bind a dispatched subagent (CRT-2D7X establishes this from the other direction), so the fix has a real anchor: the binding mechanism exists, it simply does not cover execution.

CRT-8K6M.title: critic: risk_surfaces has no discovery question and no registry row

sections.Problem: `risk_surfaces:` decides review depth for every onboarded repo, and the only route to declaring it is a product owner reading a comment block in a template they may never open.
sections.Repro: Search `discovery.md` for the question that would produce the answer — *where would a missed defect cost you most?*
sections.Actual: It is not asked. Pipeline coverage checked surface by surface: Artifact **present**, Builder **present**, Critic **present** (code-derived), Discovery **absent**. `cross-cutting-concerns.md` gained rows for both record-lint concerns in the same bundle and none for this one, so it is not discoverable through the registry either.
sections.Expected: Discovery asks the question, and the concern has a registry row.
sections.Evidence: **The absent leg is the load-bearing one.** An unasked question is an unanswered one, and the fallback is silent **by design**: a repo declaring no risk surfaces keeps the older file-count rule **forever**, with nothing ever prompting it to reconsider. That fallback is correct — it is what made the roster change safe to ship on this repo's evidence alone (CRT-2W8J) — but it converts a missing discovery question from a documentation nicety into the thing that decides review depth for every onboarded product.

COV-4H7N.title: gates: a doc-only PR can silently break a repo-coupled test

sections.Problem: Both the doc-only fast-path and `test-status`'s judgeable-path classifier assume non-code files cannot change test outcomes. Repo-coupled (**non-hermetic**) tests read committed state and docs, so a `.prawduct/*` edit **can** flip a test red.
sections.Repro: PR #125 changed only `.prawduct/*.md` plus `project-state.yaml`.
sections.Actual: `check-pr-doc-only` reported doc-only (skipping Critic, PR review and the suite) **and** `test-status` reported current — while `tests/test_norm_probes.py::TestSilentAgainstThisRepo` reads the **live** `project-state.yaml`, so ratifying the registry silently broke develop. Caught only on the next unrelated branch's suite run.
sections.Expected: One of: treat files a non-hermetic test reads as judgeable; run the suite on doc-only PRs when repo-coupled tests exist; or inventory and narrow the non-hermetic tests so the assumption becomes true.
sections.Evidence: **This is a hard constraint on COV-2P7F, which pushes the opposite direction.** That item wants `.prawduct/**` treated as governance-only so a metadata edit escapes full gates; this is the counterexample proving a **blanket** exemption is unsound while non-hermetic tests exist — exempting `project-state.yaml` from the suite is exactly what let #125 break silently. Any such design must account for this: the safe exemption is narrower than "all of `.prawduct/**`", or the suite/inventory fix lands first.

GOV-2R8W.title: gates: the session Critic gate's firing guard is porcelain-based

sections.Problem: The v3 session-end Critic gate still fires on `git_has_session_changes`, a porcelain check, while the question it documents is about the session's **tree span**.
sections.Repro: A session that commits all of its work, then reaches session end with a clean porcelain.
sections.Actual: The gate never runs, so the session never gets the Q2 composition verdict — *do recorded reviews cover the session's tree span?*
sections.Expected: The guard fires when the session's tree span is non-empty, not only when porcelain is dirty.
sections.Evidence: **v2-parity jurisdiction** — the PR gate still covers the branch — so this is a documented-span-wider-than-firing-guard mismatch rather than an escape. Filed as a NOTE from the kernel-v3 chunk 04 Critic review. Candidate for a later constituent plan of the kernel program.

GOV-6H4P.title: gates: two v3 session-gate advisory surfaces are coarser than the gate

sections.Problem: Two advisory surfaces report less than the blocking gate knows.
sections.Repro: Trigger a schema-ahead or error verdict, and separately run a session in one worktree while another has a newer review fact.
sections.Actual: (a) `briefing._check_previous_session_gates` collapses error and schema-ahead verdicts into "Critic review not recorded", **hiding the update-plugin remedy** from the session-start advisory. (b) Gate 2.5's synthesis advisory reads the **clone-global** latest review fact, so another worktree's review steers this session's advisory.
sections.Expected: The briefing differentiates the verdicts, and the synthesis advisory keys its fact read to the session's own worktree and branch.
sections.Evidence: **Both are advisory-only — the blocking gate is unaffected.** Filed as a NOTE from the kernel-v3 chunk 04 Critic review. (b) is the same clone-global-vs-worktree confusion the evidence store's shared design makes easy to reach.

BLD-7W2J.title: governance: single-slot active_build_plan vs parallel in-flight plans

sections.Problem: Two concurrent feature branches each set the one `active_build_plan` pointer, guaranteeing a same-line merge conflict on develop — after which one plan is invisible to every pointer-resolved governance surface (stop hook, `infer-critic-mode`, `verify-chunk-refs`) until repointed.
sections.Proposed change: - Model multi-plan state — a plan list, or per-branch resolution — or document the parallel-branch convention
sections.Acceptance: - [ ] Two in-flight plans do not make either invisible to governance
sections.Scope-out: The release-side multi-plan problem, already solved by REL-4T8N (`regen-views` enumerates change-log scopes rather than the pointer). Only the **in-flight** pointer remains single-slot.
sections.Evidence: `planning.md`'s "Plan lifecycle on gitflow" paragraph covers only the *serial* release-pending case. Tracked build plans plus scope-named files make parallel plans **more** likely, not less. Note CRT-4V8P is the same pointer's other failure mode — a *correctly set* pointer being read by work it does not govern — so a design here should cover both readings.

GOV-9T2K.title: governance: upgrading consumers keep old plugin cache directories

sections.Problem: Plugin caches are version-keyed, and updating leaves the old version's directory on disk — including prawduct's own internal state.
sections.Repro: Install v3.1.0 into an isolated config dir, advance the source, then run `claude plugin marketplace update` and `claude plugin update`.
sections.Actual: The active plugin correctly becomes the clean tree, but the old directory is **retained** with all 314 files including prawduct's backlog, learnings, change-log, build plans and test suite. `claude plugin prune` does not remove it.
sections.Expected: `/prawduct:doctor` globs `~/.claude*/plugins/cache/<plugin>/`, reports version directories below the running version, and prints the delete command.
sections.Evidence: **Measured on a real machine, and worse than first assumed: caches are per *config directory*, not per machine.** Four config dirs, **16 version directories, ~90 MB**, each pre-v3.1.1 copy still holding prawduct's `.prawduct/`, `tests/` and `documentation/` — the exact contamination v3.1.1 removes. The owner confirms multiple profiles is their normal setup, so this is routine, not an edge case. Two consequences: the remediation is not a single `rm`, and a consumer will not necessarily know how many profiles they have. **That strengthens the doctor option over upstream research** — it needs no upstream mechanism and works regardless of whether Claude Code ever prunes. Impact raised M→L: not tidiness, but another product's requirements sitting readable in every profile.

REL-3M7K.title: release: wire the root CHANGELOG.md headline into release-prep

sections.Problem: Release-prep updates the `.prawduct/` views but not the consumer-facing root `CHANGELOG.md`, so the headline is a forgettable hand step — and releases have tagged without a green suite.
sections.Repro: Run release-prep and then check `CHANGELOG.md` for the new version.
sections.Actual: v2.1.6 was tagged and version-bumped with no headline, leaving develop **RED** on `test_changelog_has_current_version_entry` since the release — i.e. **v2.1.6 shipped on a red suite**. Recurred at v3.0.4, backfilled out-of-band.
sections.Expected: The headline is wired into the release-promotion flow — or generated from the `release=` change-log tag the way release-notes are — and release-prep **refuses to bump or tag on a non-green suite**.
sections.Evidence: Impact raised M→L on the recurrence: at this cadence the cost — releases shipping with a missing or late headline, and the CHANGELOG-current-version test flapping — clearly exceeds the small effort of wiring it, and the fix is still unbuilt. Identical failure mode across at least three occurrences.

SEC-4Q7H.title: security: audit auth/authz as a holistic cross-cutting concern

sections.Problem: Auth was deliberately not duplicated into the API-design concern because it belongs to the Security pipeline. That placement needs confirming rather than assuming.
sections.Proposed change: - Trace auth and authz across the **full** pipeline — discovery structural detection, the security-model artifact, builder guidance, Critic checks — and confirm it is treated coherently across ALL surfaces (API, human-interface, multi-party, unattended) rather than ad-hoc per surface
sections.Acceptance: - [ ] Either coverage is confirmed sound, or the gaps are named
sections.Scope-out: Building anything. This is an audit; route it through discovery to advance the stage.
sections.Evidence: Look specifically for: object-level authorization / BOLA (OWASP API Top 10 #1); session vs token models; multi-party trust-boundary enforcement; and whether the security-model template prompts auth decisions strongly enough. Likely a follow-on to the api-design work.

TEL-2B6K.title: telemetry: gate.blocked/probe.fired events, and the disposition join

sections.Problem: The ledger records `review.critic`/`review.pr` only, so proportionality tuning cannot answer how often each gate blocked, which probes fire and where, or whether findings were acted on.
sections.Proposed change:
- Add `gate.blocked` / `probe.fired` event kinds (the schema already reserves unknown-kind forward-compat)
- Close the join so disposition facts reach actionable-rate reporting
sections.Acceptance:
- [ ] `review-stats`' actionable-rate reflects **dispositions**, not severity-presence
- [ ] Gate-event volume control is decided
sections.Scope-out: The disposition **record**, which landed 2026-07-29 as the `disposition` fact kind (`lib/dispositions.py`, append-only, plus `disposition` and `render-dispositions`). The capture design question is answered.
sections.Evidence: **The join is newly identified and was NOT part of the original filing: the two halves landed in different stores and neither reads the other.** `dispositions.py` writes to the **evidence store**; `review-stats` reads the **governance ledger** and derives `actionable` from severity presence. So the dishonest metric part (b) existed to fix is **still exactly as dishonest**, and the facts that would make it honest sit in a store `review-stats` never opens. **Fix shape is a real fork**: either `review-stats` grows an evidence-store read with a severity fallback for historical findings, or the census and review-stats converge into one surface — and having `review-stats` read two stores with different keying and lifetimes is the cross-store coupling this repo has been reducing, so "converge the reports" may be cheaper.

TEL-7A4X.title: telemetry: aggregate review cost and yield across governed products

sections.Problem: Proportionality tuning is per-project, so there is no evidence base for framework-wide decisions — which products' chunk reviews yield nothing, where escalation pays.
sections.Proposed change: - An aggregator that scans known product directories, collects each repo's `review-stats --json`, and renders review wall-clock and actionable-finding rate by mode, model and project
sections.Acceptance: - [ ] A cross-project view exists and is evidence-driven
sections.Scope-out: Building before the requirements settle. Three are open: where the aggregate view lives (skill vs doc vs janitor section), product opt-in and privacy posture (ledgers are gitignored local state), and whether differing plugin versions skew comparability.
sections.Evidence: **UNBLOCKED** — review-proportionality chunks 02 and 03 both shipped in v2.1.0, so the `review-stats --json` stable machine shape (top-level `schema_version`/`project`/`generated_at`) exists and is the integration point. Reuse the same product-directory discovery the "reviewing product feedback" route uses for `learnings.md`. Next step is the open requirements, not code.

JNT-4R2M.title: janitor: the skill instructs a hook subcommand it has no grant for

sections.Problem: `skills/janitor/SKILL.md` instructs *"Run `prawduct-hook review-stats`"*, and its `allowed-tools` carries no grant covering `review-stats` in either invocation form.
sections.Repro: Run the janitor in a plugin-governed product repo, where the hook is only reachable as `prawduct-hook`.
sections.Actual: The call is unrunnable there. **It is runnable in this self-hosted checkout**, because janitor holds `Bash(python3 *)` — which is exactly why the gap stayed invisible while dogfooding: every local janitor run reached the hook by the self-hosted path.
sections.Expected: Grant **both** forms — `Bash(prawduct-hook review-stats*)` and `Bash(python3 bin/prawduct-hook review-stats*)` — scoped to the subcommands the janitor actually instructs.
sections.Evidence: **Verified as an outlier, not a design position**: every sibling skill that instructs a hook call carries the matching scoped grant — advisory, backlog, critic (nine), doctor (five), migrate, onboard, pr (seven), repo-disable. The only other grant-less skills instruct no hook calls at all. **Evidence corrected at PR review**: Chunk 04 later added two `backlog` grants to that exact line, so this is now a *missing subcommand* gap rather than a missing-grant-entirely one — which makes it more clearly an oversight, since the same line was edited without `review-stats` being noticed. **Landing only the bare form recreates half the gap.** `skills/backlog/SKILL.md:7` is the house precedent.

JNT-5K3W.title: janitor: surface orphaned prawduct-namespace labels, never delete them

sections.Problem: The facet mutators **provision** namespaced labels on demand and never garbage-collect them, so a repo accumulates `area:*` / `kind:*` / `stage:*` labels with zero issues — typos, renamed areas, abandoned values — cluttering the label picker for humans filing by hand.
sections.Proposed change:
- A janitor Backlog Health sub-check listing `prawduct`-namespace labels with a zero issue count, framed as *"candidates for deletion — delete in the GitHub UI if you agree"*
- Read-only; no adapter write path
sections.Acceptance: - [ ] Zero-issue namespaced labels are surfaced, and nothing is deleted automatically
sections.Scope-out: **Auto-deletion, categorically.** `lib/backlog/provision.py` is deliberately **create-only** (PROV-1: existing labels are never modified) precisely so the taxonomy **coexists** with labels humans and other tools own (GV6). An automatic GC would violate that guarantee the first time it met a zero-issue label another workflow owns — and label deletion is not recoverable through the adapter.
sections.Evidence: Only the namespaces prawduct provisions are ever listed — never a bare label. Surfaced by the samsung-frame-art-loader Phase 1 dogfood.

JNT-8E3P.title: janitor: compute the Norm Health erosion measurements

sections.Problem: The Norm Health sweep measures erosion by hand — the janitor searches for violation sites per norm and manually records a point-in-time measurement under `norm_health:` so the next sweep sees a trend.
sections.Proposed change: - Derive violation-site counting and trending from code: per-norm search signal → counts → trend deltas against the recorded history
sections.Acceptance: - [ ] Erosion numbers are derived rather than hand-counted, so they are comparable across runs
sections.Scope-out: Automating norms that cannot declare a machine-checkable signal. **Most norms carry prose-only constraints**, so a v1 likely scopes to those that can declare one, with the manual path remaining for the rest.
sections.Evidence: The trajectory failure the theme exists to catch — many individually-defensible exceptions summing to a dead norm — becomes mechanical only once the numbers are comparable. Needs a design pass on **how a norm declares its violation signal** (e.g. a search pattern on its Enforcement row).

JNT-9R2K.title: janitor: move the theme taxonomy out and close the Step 2.5→7 loop

sections.Problem: Three defects in one skill: the nine investigation themes are ~100 lines (about half the skill) read once per run; the linkage from Step 2.5's findings to Step 7's actions is implicit; and the "fresh eyes" framing gives no instruction for the case it most needs one.
sections.Proposed change:
- Move theme details to a bundled companion file — the pattern the Critic already uses with `review-protocol.md` — and keep `SKILL.md` as dispatcher plus process
- State that Step 2.5 Backlog Health emits **read-only NOTE findings** and Step 7 Reconcile is where those drive `/prawduct:backlog update` calls
- Reframe "fresh eyes" toward pattern-detection and infer-and-confirm, and say what to do when the user **cannot** confirm a preference divergence: **file a backlog item rather than resolving unilaterally**
sections.Acceptance: - [ ] The skill body is dispatcher-plus-process and the 2.5→7 linkage is explicit
sections.Scope-out: Changing what the themes are.
sections.Evidence: From the 2026-06-09 framework review (skills agent). The companion-file split also serves the payload-cost argument CRT-5W3P makes for the Critic's own files.

JNT-9R2K.note: Three unrelated defects in one skill: payload relocation, an implicit step linkage, and a framing fix.

LRN-2D7Q.title: learnings: ship a framework corpus products read at query time

sections.Problem: `/prawduct:learnings` reads only `.prawduct/learnings.md` and `learnings-detail.md`, both product-local. A product onboarding today inherits the methodology and the gates and **none of the rules prawduct paid for** — every onboarded product re-learns from zero.
sections.Proposed change:
- A plugin-shipped corpus **read at query time**, never copied into the product at onboard
- Kept a **distinct store** from the product's own learnings, surfaced together and **labelled by origin**
sections.Acceptance:
- [ ] A rule may carry `scope=general` only if **all three** generality tests hold: stack-agnostic; not about prawduct internals; about building software with an agent rather than about this codebase
- [ ] Query-time token cost is checked against a corpus several times today's size
sections.Scope-out: **Hoist-at-onboard — ruled out.** The whole value is that the corpus keeps updating as the framework learns; a copy taken at onboard freezes at that day's vintage, so every product runs a different one and none ever gets a correction.
sections.Evidence: **The sharpest case is the text-anchored-edit rule**, and it is the argument that this is a defect rather than a nice-to-have: it describes a defect *the agent's own `Edit` tool manufactures in every repo*, which a product cannot learn independently because it does not present as a tool problem — it presents as a mystery regression. **Only one promotion path exists today and it is narrow**: code-delivered directives do ship and do fire, so the capability is proven, but that path only covers a rule with a **moment** some command runs at. **The methodology-guide path is effectively closed** — `building.md` and `session-digest.md` are at their ceilings, so adding a rule costs an existing one. **Reconciled with MET-8K4R**: norms are **ratifiable**, so a copy is the point; learnings are **knowledge**, so a copy is pure staleness. Same principle, two kinds of thing. **Still open**: the promotion *mechanism* — a hand-authored file vs a rendered derived view are different builds.

LRN-2M8V.title: learnings: learnings-detail.md is an unbounded sink with no route out

sections.Problem: Every compaction mechanism the framework has relieves `learnings.md` by moving bytes **into** the detail file, and nothing ever removes anything from it or measures it.
sections.Repro: `wc -c .prawduct/learnings-detail.md` — re-derive rather than citing digits.
sections.Actual: ~338KB across 175 headings, of which the terminal Historical section is ~37KB. It gained roughly 12KB in a single chunk. `reflection.md` states the design in terms: *"No size constraint."*
sections.Expected: A **route out** — the Historical section as its own file the skill reads only when a lookup misses; a date-partitioned archive; or an index the skill seeks into.
sections.Evidence: **The cost is real rather than notional**: `/prawduct:learnings` reads **both** files on every lookup, and the forked context bounds what comes *back*, not what is *read*. LRN-2D7Q flags exactly this bound as an open risk for a shipped general corpus and says it needs checking against a corpus several times today's size — **this file is that corpus at that size, today.** **NOT a prune**: nothing here should be deleted, and LRN-4K8T's conservation check (refuse to write unless every moved byte is found in the destination) should survive whatever ships. `stage: design` because the answer depends on how the skill queries, and that decision should be taken **once for both files**. LRN-6C2X constrains any split — the same-heading pairing must survive it — and MET-4P9C owns the "No size constraint" line.

LRN-6C2X.title: learnings: the same-heading pairing invariant has nothing enforcing it

sections.Problem: `learnings.md`'s own header states the invariant — each entry's full narrative lives in `learnings-detail.md` **under the same heading** — and nothing checks it.
sections.Repro: Check all rules in `learnings.md` for an exactly-matching detail heading.
sections.Actual: Five have no detail section. Four have no prefix match at all; the fifth **has** one whose heading has **DRIFTED** out of exact match — and that second failure mode is the more interesting one, because the pairing breaks silently whenever either heading is edited without the other.
